title: Sr. Manufacturing HW Eng, AI/ML & Storage server development
descriptionHtml:
Team Introduction
AWS Hardware Engineering designs and delivers next-generation cloud infrastructure at global scale. Our Storage & AI/ML Manufacturing team owns the manufacturing engineering lifecycle for custom server platforms — from early design engagement and NPI execution through volume production, supplier quality, and continuous improvement. We partner with ODM/JDM design and manufacturing partners across a global network to deliver hardware at scale with exceptional quality.

We are seeking a Cloud Hardware Development Engineer (Manufacturing) to drive manufacturing excellence across our server portfolio. Depending on the specific role, you will own NPI execution, manufacturing process quality, test and diagnostic development, automation strategy, DFx standards, or reliability engineering — ensuring our platforms launch on time, at quality, and at scale. You will work directly with hardware design teams, ODM/CM partners, and cross-functional stakeholders to close the loop between design intent and manufacturing execution.
What You Will Do
You will own manufacturing engineering for cloud storage server platforms deployed at global scale. Your work spans the full product lifecycle: engaging early with design teams on manufacturability, driving NPI builds through EVT/DVT/PVT at partner sites, building quality systems and test strategies that scale across a multi-ODM network, and continuously improving yield, throughput, and cost. When a new storage platform launches into production, the manufacturing readiness, quality gates, reliability, and process controls are yours. You treat manufacturing risk probabilistically — planning to distributions, not point estimates.
Why You Will Love It
The storage infrastructure you manufacture powers exabytes of customer data across AWS. You will see your process decisions, quality systems, and automation initiatives scale to millions of units across a global manufacturing network. The team is deeply technical, high-trust, and moves fast — you own your domain end to end, from early DFx engagement through production ramp and fleet operations.
 
The Ideal Candidate
You think across the full manufacturing stack — from PCBA assembly and SMT process control to system-level integration and rack deployment. You are as comfortable on an ODM production floor as you are analyzing yield data or reviewing a DFx scorecard. You drive quality through data and structured problem-solving, not assumption. You hold manufacturing partners to the same standard you hold yourself, and you communicate with clarity across engineering, operations, and leadership. You look for automation and ML-assisted approaches to solve complex issues.


Key job responsibilities
Process Quality & Supplier Management
• Lead and oversee quality control processes across Contract Manufacturers (CM), Original Design Manufacturers (ODM), and component vendors
• Own PFMEAs, Control Plans, and process flows from NPI startup through end of life
• Drive Root Cause Corrective Action (RCCA) for manufacturing blockers, yield detractors, and quality escapes
• Execute Test Rack Inspections and OK2Ship checklists; issue quality alerts, deviations, and ship-holds as required
• Conduct factory audits and supplier quality assessments across the ODM/vendor network
• Scale up manufacturing processes across a global network ensuring consistent quality and throughput targets
Manufacturing Test, Diagnostics & Debug
• Design, develop, and maintain manufacturing test software and diagnostic tools deployed at ODM/CM lines
• Debug complex system-level failures at the manufacturing line across compute, storage, networking, power, and thermal domains
• Perform root cause analysis correlating across firmware, kernel, driver, PCIe, signal integrity, and physical layers to isolate faults
• Build automation that reduces manual triage — enabling faster fault isolation and higher first-pass yield
• Develop and optimize system-level test flows (BFT, functional test, stress test, burn-in) for storage server platforms
• Analyze test data and yield trends to identify systemic issues; drive design and process improvements
 
Automation & Controls
• Own automation strategy, equipment selection, and ROI justification for manufacturing line automation
• Develop and implement manufacturing test fixtures at the server and rack level
• Define processes around assembly and test fixtures to ensure consistent, repeatable results
• Research and implement automation techniques to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce human intervention
• Scale up tooling, fixturing, and process across the manufacturing network; standardize across multiple ODM sites
• Build, manage, and deploy CI/CD pipelines for rapid deployment of test code to manufacturing environments
DFx, Standards & Cross-Program Reuse
• Lead DFx reviews (DFM/DFA/DFT) leveraging mechanical CAD models, gerber files, and mock-up samples; drive design improvements in partnership with hardware engineering
• Develop and maintain DFx scorecards and NPI playbooks that capture cross-program learnings
• Define manufacturing engineering standards and design best practices adopted across teams and partner organizations
• Drive cross-vertical knowledge reuse — ensuring lessons from one program propagate to others
• Collaborate on manufacturing simulation, digital twin, and throughput modeling initiatives
• Own the interface between design intent and manufacturing execution for DFx requirements
Reliability & Failure Analysis
• Own cross-program reliability coverage, matrixed to verticals on demand
• Monitor fleet quality metrics post-launch: server-level annualized failure rates and component-level failure modes
• Correlate component-level failure data with manufacturing lot information to identify systemic issues
• Partner with test and fleet health teams to ensure manufacturing diagnostics align with production monitoring and field failure analysis
• Drive design or process changes for current and future platforms based on operational telemetry
• Perform risk assessment, mitigation, and change management throughout the product lifecycle


A day in the life
You start the day analyzing cross-program yield trends, identifying a common failure mode across two verticals that points to a shared component vendor issue. Mid-morning, you facilitate a DFx standards review — updating the NPI playbook with lessons from the latest program launch. In the afternoon, you run a throughput simulation for an upcoming automation investment, building the ROI case for leadership. You end the day reviewing reliability data with the fleet health team, feeding findings back into manufacturing process controls for the current and next-generation platforms. You are willing to travel domestically 4+ times per year. You are willing to travel internationally 2+ times per year.

About the team
The Storage AI/ML Manufacturing team is part of AWS Hardware Engineering — the organization that designs, delivers, and sustains the server and storage hardware behind every AWS service. We own manufacturing engineering for AWS custom storage server platforms, from concept through volume production and fleet-scale operations.

We operate as a Hybrid organization: program-dedicated manufacturing engineers embed in each product vertical for tight NPI alignment, while strategic and portfolio-shared roles centralize under a Manufacturing Lead for cross-program leverage. This structure gives you deep program ownership and broad technical community — whether you sit in a vertical driving a specific product launch or in the central team driving standards, automation, and reliability across the portfolio.

Located in Cupertino / Seattle / Denver, we collaborate with global development teams and ODM partners to deliver storage infrastructure deployed in datacenters worldwide. We move fast with small, empowered teams delivering end to end.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or above in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or Business Administration
- Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Chemical, Industrial or Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline
- 6+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in NPI, process development, or production engineering within semiconductor, server/datacenter hardware, electronics, or high-tech manufacturing
- 3+ years of end-to-end NPI product delivery experience from concept through volume production
- Hands-on experience with SMT assembly processes/PCB fabrication, or industrial automation or robotics
- Strong data analysis skills using statistical tools (JMP, Minitab, Excel, Python) to drive data-driven decisions
- Experience driving quality and schedule execution at multinational JDM, ODM, CM, and supplier partners

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Manufacturing, Chemical, Mechanical, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of relevant industry experience spanning semiconductor equipment, wafer fab operations, advanced packaging, or high-volume server/networking hardware manufacturing
- Experience with Stoarge or GPU-based server or accelerator platform manufacturing
- Experience with PLC programming, industrial controls, and automated test equipment (ATE) in production; ability to troubleshoot PLC-controlled systems and robotic work cells
- Process tool ownership including process-of-record (POR), recipe management, equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), and OEE tracking for tools such as reflow ovens, pick-and-place, or AOI/AXI
- Experience with DOE (Design of Experiments), MSA (Measurement System Analysis), GR&R studies, and process capability analysis in a production setting
- Track record of driving yield improvement, DFx, PFMEA, and cost optimization through automation and process engineering

title: Data Center Material Associate, IT Services (Warehouse)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's IT Services (ITS) team is seeking a detail-oriented Data Center Material Associate, Warehouse (Reverse Logistics) to support the recovery, tracking, and lifecycle management of IT assets within our India operations. In this role, you will own the end-to-end reverse-logistics journey for IT equipment — ensuring that devices are retrieved, verified, and processed accurately as employees transition out of the organization.

You will act as the central coordination point between internal stakeholders, logistics partners, and asset-management systems to drive timely asset returns and maintain a high IT-clearance completion rate. The position combines operational execution, data accuracy, and strong communication, working within established policies and standard operating procedures.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys structured, process-driven work with measurable outcomes. You will contribute directly to inventory accuracy, cost avoidance, and compliance goals while gaining exposure to large-scale operations, logistics coordination, and IT asset-management tooling. The ideal candidate is organized, dependable, and comfortable managing a steady volume of cases, following up persistently, and resolving discrepancies through collaboration. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and take pride in operational excellence, we encourage you to apply.

Key job responsibilities
- Asset recovery coordination: Manage the day-to-day queue of reverse-logistics cases, ensuring IT assets are recovered promptly and tracked through each stage of the return process.

- Stakeholder communication: Send structured notifications and reminders to relevant stakeholders, follow up on pending returns, and respond to queries in a professional, timely manner.

- Logistics partner coordination: Work with third-party logistics providers to schedule pickups, confirm shipments, and validate receipt of assets at designated locations.

- Data accuracy & tracking: Maintain accurate records of asset status, movements, and discrepancies using asset-management and tracking tools; reconcile data to ensure inventory integrity.

- Discrepancy resolution: Identify and resolve mismatches, missing items, or tagging errors by collaborating with internal teams and following defined escalation paths.

- Clearance & compliance: Support IT-clearance workflows and ensure processes adhere to organizational policies and audit requirements.

- Reporting: Prepare and share regular status updates and queue reports to provide visibility into operational performance and open items.

- Process improvement: Identify recurring issues and suggest improvements to increase efficiency, reduce turnaround time, and improve the overall return experience.

- Documentation: Maintain clear, organized records to support traceability and knowledge continuity across the team.

A day in the life
On a typical day, you will review and prioritize the reverse-logistics case queue, send notifications and follow-up reminders for pending asset returns, and coordinate pickups and shipments with logistics partners. You will update asset-tracking systems with current statuses, confirm receipts, and reconcile any data discrepancies. Part of your day involves responding to stakeholder queries, escalating blocked cases through defined channels, and verifying that recovered assets are correctly logged and processed. Prepare short status updates summarizing queue health and open items. Throughout, you will apply standard operating procedures to keep cases moving and ensure accuracy, timeliness, and compliance.

About the team
You will join the **ITS Reverse Logistics team**, a group dedicated to managing the recovery and lifecycle of IT assets across Amazon's India operations. The team ensures that equipment is efficiently returned, verified, and processed as employees transition, directly supporting inventory accuracy, cost efficiency, and compliance goals. We work closely with internal IT, logistics partner and logistics partners, using modern asset-management and tracking tools to coordinate a high volume of cases at scale. The team values accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvement, and offers a collaborative, process-driven environment where your contributions have a clear, measurable impact on operational performance.

Basic qualifications

- Speak, write, and read fluently in English, and have the ability to take direction in English
- Experience with Microsoft Office products and applications
- Experience managing work and priorities through a ticketing system and coordination with Manager
- 1+ years of shipping & receiving, inventory and warehousing practices experience
- Education qualification : Graduate

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in courier industry, or experience in logistics

descriptionHtml:

You will act as a trusted technical advisor, helping customers accelerate their cloud adoption — from migration and modernization to cloud-native applications and emerging technologies such as generative AI and agentic AI. A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing architecture designs for a customer's cloud migration, then join a working session with their engineering team to refine a data warehousing solution. title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.



Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.



A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

It's a place where your paycheck goes further and there's room to build a life, not just a career.

title: Manager, Device Mgmt Team, Amazon Devices Beta Team
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s Device Services & Operations organization is seeking a dynamic, results-oriented leader to manage the Device Management Team (DMT) — the team responsible for the complete prototype device lifecycle across all Amazon consumer device families. This is a high-impact, high-visibility operations leadership role that sits at the intersection of hardware development, supply chain logistics, and cross-functional program execution within one of the world’s most innovative consumer electronics organizations.

As DMT Manager, you will lead a globally distributed team of approximately 10 team members spanning three sites: Seattle (primary), Munich, and Chennai. Your team owns the end-to-end prototype device lifecycle — from procurement and inbound logistics through inventory management, allocation and distribution, beta program support, and device destruction. This lifecycle touches every Amazon device family, including Alexa, Fire TV, Tablet, Kindle E-reader, Ring, Blink, Eero, Leo (Project Kuiper), V-Care, and Smart Home products. The breadth of product lines and the global nature of operations create a uniquely challenging and rewarding management opportunity.

You will be responsible for managing a diverse team that includes Program Managers, Device Associates, and Administrative Support staff operating across multiple time zones (Pacific, Central European, and India Standard Time). Your direct reports include operations leads in each geography, a PVT Procurement and Budget lead, an Inbound Lead, Outbound Leads in both Seattle and Munich, and specialized roles in device flashing and customer returns. You will need to develop strong deputies in each location to ensure operational continuity during non-overlapping business hours, while fostering a cohesive team culture that transcends geographic boundaries.

The role carries significant stakeholder management responsibilities. You will interface regularly with product teams across Alexa, Fire TV, Ring/Blink, Tablet, E-reader, Leo, V-Care, and Smart Home — each with distinct working styles, escalation tendencies, and volume profiles. Beta program coordination is the most complex and escalation-prone workstream, requiring careful negotiation between product team timelines and DMT operational capacity. Allocations represent the highest throughput function, and managing competing priorities across product lines during peak season (typically April through September) demands sophisticated prioritization skills and the confidence to push back when necessary.

Operational reporting is a core element of this role. You will own the Weekly Business Review (WBR) cadence, ensuring timely and accurate reporting of operational metrics every Wednesday. You will also maintain a regular weekly reporting cadence with senior leadership. The ability to synthesize complex operational data into clear, actionable narratives for director-level and VP-level audiences is essential.

This role also includes ownership of several high-priority strategic initiatives. You will drive the DBS (Device Build System) integration — a platform dependency that underpins three of the team’s annual goals: increasing operations capacity, increasing PM capacity through global functional consolidation, and improving quality by reducing defects per thousand opportunities (DPTO). You will also oversee a VP-directed initiative to reduce PVT device ordering volumes and champion the KFlex integration pilot to modernize the team’s tooling and workflow automation.

Perhaps most critically, this role requires a people-first leader who can build team morale. The team is currently under significant workload pressure, and team members have historically struggled to set boundaries with stakeholders. You must create a culture where it is safe to push back, establish clear prioritization frameworks, and visibly advocate upward for headcount relief and process improvements. Protecting the team from unreasonable demands — while maintaining strong partnerships with product teams — is the defining leadership challenge of this position.

The ideal candidate brings experience managing geographically distributed operations teams in a fast-paced hardware or technology environment. You should be comfortable with ambiguity, skilled at managing competing priorities under resource constraints, and energized by the challenge of optimizing prototype logistics at global scale. Familiarity with device lifecycle management, prototype operations, or consumer electronics supply chain is strongly preferred.

Key job responsibilities
Lead and develop a globally distributed team of ~10 across Seattle, Munich, and Chennai, fostering a collaborative, resilient culture despite timezone challenges and high operational tempo.

Own the end-to-end prototype device lifecycle — procurement, inbound logistics, inventory management, allocation/distribution, beta program support, and destruction — across all Amazon device families.

Manage escalations and competing priorities across multiple product teams (Alexa, Fire TV, Ring/Blink, Tablet, Leo, and others), balancing urgency against team capacity with data-driven prioritization.

Drive the Weekly Business Review (WBR) process: ensure accurate, timely operational data and narrative reporting for director and VP-level leadership.

Own and advance strategic initiatives including DBS integration, KFlex pilot, global PM functional consolidation, and VP-directed PVT device ordering reduction.

Build capacity plans and workload models to anticipate peak-season surges (April–September) and advocate for staffing adjustments when operational demand exceeds capacity.

Coach team members on stakeholder management, process optimization, and career development — particularly strengthening the team’s ability to set boundaries and push back constructively on unreasonable timelines.

Establish and maintain strong cross-functional partnerships with product, engineering, logistics, and security teams while protecting the team from scope creep and last-minute demand spikes.

Champion continuous improvement by identifying automation opportunities, documenting tribal knowledge into SOPs, and cross-training team members to reduce single-points-of-failure.

A day in the life
Your morning starts early — often by 6:30 AM PT when you are online for overlap with Munich and Chennai, reviewing overnight deployment updates and triaging any escalations that came in across time zones. By 8:00 AM you are leading the global team sync (Tuesdays) or reviewing WBR data (Wednesdays), ensuring operational metrics are accurate before they reach senior leadership.

Mid-morning shifts to stakeholder engagement: a product team has moved up an in-hand date for a beta deployment, another needs expedited allocations for a launch milestone. You negotiate trade-offs, re-sequence the queue, and coach your team on when to absorb the request and when to push back. The afternoon brings 1:1s with your reports, where you discuss career growth alongside operational blockers. Between meetings, you check on the KFlex pilot, review a hire requisition for a critical backfill, and Slack your manager a status update. No two days are identical — but the pace is always high.

About the team
The Device Management Team (DMT) operates within the Beta organization under Amazon’s DevicesTech division. DMT is the operational backbone of prototype device management — every device that moves through the pre-launch pipeline passes through this team’s hands.

With team members across Seattle, Munich, and Chennai, DMT supports all Amazon device families including Alexa, Fire TV, Kindle, Ring, Blink, Eero, and emerging programs like Project Kuiper (Leo). The team prides itself on a collaborative, roll-up-your-sleeves culture where everyone supports each other across functions and geographies. It is a team that consistently delivers under pressure and takes genuine pride in its work — and it deserves a leader who will invest in its people as much as its processes.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of team management experience
- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- 3+ years of delivering cross functional projects experience
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

Preferred qualifications

- Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
- Experience in data mining, data management, reporting, and SQL queries

title: Sr. AI/ML Specialist Solutions Architect, AGS-WWSO NAMER Specialist Solutions Architects
descriptionHtml:
AWS Global Sales drives adoption of the AWS cloud worldwide, enabling customers of all sizes to innovate and expand in the cloud. Our team empowers every customer to grow by providing tailored service, unmatched technology, and committed support. We dive deep to understand each customer's unique challenges, then craft innovative solutions that accelerate their success. This customer-first approach is how we built the world's most adopted cloud. Join us and help us grow.

Are you passionate about Generative AI, Agentic AI, and Machine Learning? Are you passionate about helping customers design and build solutions leveraging the most comprehensive GenAI/ML platform available? Come join us!

At Amazon, we've been investing deeply in artificial intelligence for over 25 years, and many of the capabilities customers experience in our products are driven by machine learning. Amazon.com's recommendations engine is driven by ML, as are the paths that optimize robotic picking routes in our fulfillment centers. Our supply chain, forecasting, and capacity planning are informed by ML algorithms. Alexa is fueled by Natural Language Understanding and Automated Speech Recognition with deep learning. More recently, we've put generative AI at the core of every Amazon business, from coding assistants that help our developers ship faster, to AI agents that automate complex operational workflows, to foundation models that power entirely new customer experiences. We have thousands of engineers at Amazon committed to pushing the frontier of AI, and it's a big part of our heritage.

Within AWS, we bring that knowledge and capability to customers through three layers of the AI stack: 1) AI Infrastructure with purpose-built chips like AWS Trainium and Inferentia, GPU-powered instances, and optimized frameworks like PyTorch and JAX, 2) AI/ML Platforms including Amazon Bedrock for building generative AI applications with foundation models, agents, guardrails, and knowledge bases, and Amazon SageMaker AI for end-to-end model building, training, and deployment, and 3) AI Application Services like Amazon Quick and Kiro (developer and business productivity), Amazon Nova foundation models, Amazon Transcribe, Amazon Textract, Amazon Comprehend, and Amazon Rekognition for quickly adding intelligence to applications.

AWS is looking for a GenAI/ML Solutions Architect who will be the Subject Matter Expert for helping customers in the United States design solutions leveraging our GenAI and ML services. You will work as an overlay to field sales teams, covering customers across multiple verticals and helping them architect and adopt solutions using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Nova models, and the broader AI/ML portfolio. You will design RAG architectures, agentic AI workflows, model customization strategies, responsible AI implementations, and production-scale inference pipelines. You will interact with other SAs in the field, providing guidance on their customer engagements. You will develop blog posts, reference implementations, workshops, and presentations to enable customers to fully leverage generative AI on AWS. Additionally, as the voice of the customer, you will work closely with service teams and submit product feature requests to drive the platform forward.

You must have deep technical experience working with technologies related to generative AI, machine learning, and/or deep learning. Hands-on experience building applications on foundation models (RAG pipelines, agent frameworks, prompt engineering, model evaluation, fine-tuning) is required. Building multi-agent architectures, deploying AI agents hands-on experience is required. Hands-on experience on agent platforms like Bedrock AgentCore (or equivalent in other public clouds) is strongly preferred. A deep understanding of context engineering, token optimization is needed. A strong mathematics and statistics background is preferred in addition to experience with solution architecture and production ML systems. You should be familiar with the GenAI ecosystem (model providers, orchestration frameworks, vector databases, evaluation tools) and will leverage this knowledge to help AWS customers evaluate tradeoffs and accelerate their AI adoption.

Travel up to 30% across the United States may be possible.

Key job responsibilities
Working with customers' development, data science, and AI engineering teams to deeply understand their business and technical needs. After understanding their needs, you will design solutions that make the best use of the AWS cloud platform and AWS AI/ML services including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Nova foundation models, Amazon Quick, Kiro, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Rekognition, Amazon Textract, and Amazon Transcribe.

Partner with SAs, Sales, Business Development, and the AI/ML service teams to accelerate customer adoption and revenue attainment in the AMERICAS for AWS generative AI and machine learning services, with a focus on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon SageMaker AI, and the agentic AI portfolio.

Thought Leadership: Evangelize AWS GenAI/ML services and share best practices through forums such as AWS blogs, whitepapers, reference architectures, sample code repositories, and public-speaking events such as AWS Summit, AWS re:Invent, etc.

Act as a technical liaison between customers and the AWS Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker, and broader AI/ML service teams to provide customer-driven product improvement feedback and feature requests.

Develop and support an AWS internal community of GenAI-related subject matter experts in the AMERICAS, enabling field teams to identify, qualify, and position generative AI and agentic AI opportunities with their customers.

A day in the life
Most of your time is spent working directly with customers, helping them figure out how to use generative AI and machine learning to solve real business problems.

On a given morning, you might be on a video call with a team of engineers at a large insurance company who want to build an AI agent that can process claims documents. You're sketching out an architecture on a virtual whiteboard, asking questions about their data, and helping them think through tradeoffs between different approaches. That afternoon, you're prepping a demo for a different customer who's evaluating AWS against a competitor for a conversational AI use case. Later in the week, you're on-site running a workshop where a customer's ML team is building their first retrieval-augmented generation pipeline with you guiding them through it hands-on.

You're typically focused on a single industry (think financial services, or healthcare, or manufacturing), so you build real familiarity with the problems, regulations, and data challenges in that space. You'll work with many different companies within your industry rather than being embedded at one or two for years. Some engagements last a few weeks, others stretch over a couple months, but the variety keeps things interesting.

Between customer conversations, you're building things that help others learn what you know: writing a blog post about a pattern you've seen work well, recording a short demo, or building a reference architecture that your peers across the country can reuse. You're also spending time helping other technical teams across the org understand how to spot AI/ML opportunities in their customer conversations.

Beyond the regular rhythm, some weeks bring unexpected moments that make this role special. You might get asked to present a customer success story to an audience of thousands at re:Invent, or get early access to a new service months before launch and help shape how it works based on what you've seen customers struggle with. Occasionally you'll find yourself in an executive briefing room explaining agentic AI to a Fortune 500 CTO who's deciding where to place a multi-million dollar bet.

Travel runs about 20-30%, mostly for customer workshops, executive briefings, and AWS events.

About the team
AWS Global Sales drives adoption of the AWS cloud worldwide, enabling customers of all sizes to innovate and expand in the cloud. Our team empowers every customer to grow by providing tailored service, unmatched technology, and support. We dive deep to understand each customer's unique challenges, then craft innovative solutions that accelerate their success. This customer-first approach is how we built the world's most adopted cloud. Join us and help us grow.

- 8+ years of specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) experience
- 3+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
- 10+ years of IT development or implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working with end user or developer communities

title: Software Development Engineer, ADC2S
descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Nov 12, 2026

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) control-plane services in air-gapped regions. You will help governments run secure cloud infrastructure at scale.

In this role, you will join a team of engineers who build and operate software for EC2's control plane, fleet health, and capacity operations in air-gapped cloud environments. You will own features and services from design through production, make sound trade-offs within your area, and help raise the quality of what the team ships. Commercial tooling often does not exist in isolated regions, so you will build what the team needs instead of configuring an off-the-shelf product.

The candidate selected must obtain and maintain a security clearance at the TS/SCI with polygraph level. Upon start, the selected candidate will be sponsored for a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and operate EC2 control-plane services, fleet health automation, and capacity tooling across air-gapped cloud environments.
- Own features end to end: write the design, implement and test the code, deploy it through pipelines to disconnected regions, and operate it in production, including on-call.
- Improve monitoring, alarming, and deployment safety for the services you own, and drive the fix when an operational issue reveals a gap.
- Work with partner teams and stakeholders across the air-gapped partitions to deliver shared infrastructure.
- Take part in design and code reviews, and help new engineers ramp up on the team's systems.
- Use generative artificial intelligence tools and techniques to improve automation, code quality, and team productivity.

A day in the life
You might start the morning finishing a design document for a new capacity automation feature, then review a teammate's code change to how instance lifecycle events are processed in a disconnected region. After lunch, you work with a partner team to get your change into a shared deployment pipeline, then spend the afternoon tracking down the root cause of an alarm from last night's on-call shift. You write code most days, and you are expected to propose better ways to automate capacity and remediation workflows in the systems you own.

About the team
We own the software that keeps EC2 running in the air-gapped partitions: control-plane services, fleet-health automation, and the capacity tooling our government customers depend on. We operate what we build, so the engineers who design a remediation workflow are the ones it pages. Because the commercial tooling for a problem frequently does not exist in an isolated region, you build the thing rather than configure it. The team defaults to written design documents and clear ownership boundaries, and you will work alongside engineers who are passionate about solving hard infrastructure problems in the most demanding regulated cloud environments.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree, or CSSLP (Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional)
- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience

descriptionHtml:

You will perform hands-on work across the full lifecycle of data center IT infrastructure — installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and decommissioning the servers, racks, and cabling that our customers depend on every day. title: Applied Scientist, Fauna
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an Applied Scientist to lead the development of evaluation frameworks and data collection protocols for robotic capabilities. In this role, you will focus on designing how we measure, stress-test, and improve robot behavior across a wide range of real-world tasks. Your work will play a critical role in shaping how policies are validated and how high-quality datasets are generated to accelerate system performance.
You will operate at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and human-in-the-loop systems, building the infrastructure and methodologies that connect teleoperation, evaluation, and learning. This includes developing evaluation policies, defining task structures, and contributing to operator-facing interfaces that enable scalable and reliable data collection.
The ideal candidate is highly experimental, systems-oriented, and comfortable working across software, robotics, and data pipelines, with a strong focus on turning ambiguous capability goals into measurable and actionable evaluation systems.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure robot capabilities across structured tasks, edge cases, and real-world scenarios
- Develop task definitions, success criteria, and benchmarking methodologies that enable consistent and reproducible evaluation of policies
- Create and refine data collection protocols that generate high-quality, task-relevant datasets aligned with model development needs
- Build and iterate on teleoperation workflows and operator interfaces to support efficient, reliable, and scalable data collection
- Analyze evaluation results and collected data to identify performance gaps, failure modes, and opportunities for targeted data collection
- Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate evaluation tooling, logging systems, and data pipelines into the broader robotics stack
- Stay current with advances in robotics, evaluation methodologies, and human-in-the-loop learning to continuously improve internal approaches
- Lead technical projects from conception through production deployment
- Mentor junior scientists and engineers

About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.
We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.
Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.
If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

- Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals

- Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing

descriptionHtml:

We are dreamers and inventors who come from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences to empower and inspire each other. Imagine your future with us.

Every great audiobook starts with a voice, and behind every voice is an author, a narrator, and a publisher who deserve to be paid accurately and on time. At Audible, that story comes to life on our Workday platform, where payments are just one part of a much bigger picture. Employees submit expenses, supplier invoices flow through Accounts Payable, customer billing moves through Accounts Receivable, projects are tracked from kickoff to close, and assets are managed across their lifecycle, each transaction a page in the story that has to be right.

Audible is the leading producer and provider of audio storytelling. descriptionHtml:
Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world — designed with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve individual households, schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Software and hardware changes introduce complexity, requiring coordinated cut-in planning, effectivity control, and production impact assessment across the full vehicle build flow, from Contract Manufacturer through our Factory up to Launch Operations.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
This TPM will be a core member of Amazon Leo Production's New Product Introduction team, owning the Engineering Change Implementation process end-to-end. This complex value stream governs how engineering changes, spanning both software and hardware, are reviewed, and implemented across Leo's satellite manufacturing and test operations. The role requires a demonstrated ability to drive industrial and manufacturing readiness, ensuring that engineering changes are introduced into production in a controlled, scalable, and operationally sustainable manner. The role interfaces with procurement, finance, GSE, production, warehouse, satellite design engineering, and launch operations, and is based in Redmond, WA.

The scale and complexity of engineering change management demands coordinated activities across both daily urgent activities and long-term strategic initiatives. As an adept of "working yourself out of a job," this TPM will lead the critical process and tool improvements required to protect production stability while enabling rapid innovation cycles.

Program Ownership & Governance

* Hold single-threaded ownership of the Engineering Change Control programs, managing both software and hardware change streams across Leo manufacturing and test operations
* Manage the Engineering Change Implementation Board and Software Production Implementation mechanisms, ensuring structured intake, risk classification, and approval of all changes
* Maintain the single source of truth for the change schedule, developed collaboratively with stakeholders across production, test, quality, and operations
* Serve as the primary escalation point for production-impacting changes, coordinating rapid response to quality gaps and engineering-driven stoppages
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives targeting automation of change intake, validation, and deployment workflows

Impact Assessment & Change Introduction

* Partner with engineering (design, test, manufacturing, quality) to negotiate change requirements and represent the voice of production in design reviews
* Define and track key performance indicators: software-related production disruptions, change cycle time, first-pass yield for software deployments, and change velocity

This role is highly collaborative, requiring active partnerships with cross-functional leaders across test engineering, manufacturing, software/firmware development, quality, and operations. title: Robotics Applied Scientist
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building robotic systems that combine frontier AI, sophisticated control, and advanced mechanical design to create adaptable automation capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is an opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction.

We are seeking an Applied Scientist to develop tactile- and force-driven manipulation policies for highly dexterous, multi-fingered robotic hands and grippers. In this role you will research and build policy learning algorithms that enable robotic hands to perform grasping and in-hand manipulation in unstructured, real-world environments, using touch and force feedback as first-class signals rather than afterthoughts. Much of this work is grounded in reinforcement learning.

To be successful you need to be highly motivated, dive deep, and deliver to the highest standards. You will demonstrate strong working knowledge of modern policy learning methods, with expertise in taking algorithms from simulation onto real hardware. That means being comfortable working against real physical constraints and treating sim-to-real as a core research problem rather than optimizing for benchmark numbers alone. You will work across tactile signal processing, contact-rich manipulation, sim-to-real transfer, and multi-modal sensor fusion to build robust solutions for autonomous grasping, dexterous re-orientation, and fine motor control. You will bring the desire to learn from new challenges, and the problem-solving and communication skills to work within a highly interactive and experienced team.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and train manipulation policies that leverage tactile and force feedback for dexterous grasping, in-hand manipulation, and contact-rich tasks, using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or hybrid approaches.
- Drive sim-to-real transfer, closing the gap between simulated and physical performance on real robotic hands.
- Shape objectives and control strategies with the hardware in mind, accounting for how motors and actuators actually behave: transmission ratios, torque versus power, backdrivability, and thermal limits.
- Build simulation-based and on-robot evaluation frameworks, with benchmarks and metrics that make tactile perception and policy performance systematically comparable across iterations.
- Own scientific and technical projects within the tactile sensing and manipulation workstreams, driving from research concept through deployment on physical robotic systems — and, at the senior level, set direction across a workstream.
- Collaborate with hardware, mechanical design, firmware, and controls teams — and with partner applied science organizations — to translate research advances into deployable robotic capabilities, and to inform sensor and actuator design decisions with policy-level requirements.
- Publish at top-tier venues and build collaborations with the external research community.
- Contribute to a strong scientific bar on the team through code and design review, and mentor engineers and interns working on real-world manipulation and sensing problems.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a standup alongside hardware and controls engineers reviewing overnight sim-to-real training runs on a multi-finger gripper, debugging why a grasp policy that worked in simulation is slipping on a real sensor array. Mid-morning you join the weekly tactile sensing workstream to align on sensor integration milestones and share early results from a contact-state estimator you have been prototyping. After lunch you spend a focused block iterating on a reinforcement learning reward formulation, testing variations in simulation before queuing runs on the cluster. Later you pair with a mechanical engineer to review sensor placement trade-offs on an upcoming gripper revision, then wrap the day by drafting a short experiment write-up and sketching next steps for a conference submission.

No two days look exactly the same: one week you may be collecting teleoperated demonstrations on the physical robot to seed an imitation learning pipeline; the next you could be deep in a codebase refactor to support a new tactile modality. Throughout, you balance hands-on research — writing algorithms, running experiments, analyzing data — with cross-team collaboration and mentoring. The common thread is moving from research insight to working capability on real hardware, with a tight feedback loop between simulation and the physical world.

About the team
Our is developing next-generation manipulation capabilities for highly dexterous multi-fingered grippers and hands. Our work spans tactile sensor development, manipulation policy learning, and the tight integration of sensing hardware with intelligent control software. We are building systems that can feel, adapt, and manipulate with human-level dexterity.

You will join a team working at the frontier of tactile sensing and contact-rich manipulation, helping define how robots perceive and interact with objects through touch. Because we build the hands as well as the policies that drive them, you will have a direct line to the sensor, actuator, and mechanism designs your algorithms depend on — and real influence over how they evolve. This is an opportunity to solve hard problems across perception, learning, and physical interaction alongside a team of scientists and engineers building toward real-world deployment.

Basic qualifications

- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Research or applied experience in one or more of: tactile sensing, manipulation policy learning, contact-rich manipulation, dexterous grasping, or multi-modal perception for robotics
- Experience deploying learned policies or control algorithms on physical robotic hardware

Preferred qualifications

- Experience leading technical initiatives and key deliverables
- Experience bridging research with practical engineering implementation in physical robotic systems
- Hands-on experience with modern tactile sensing hardware and tactile signal processing
- Strong publication record at major robotics/ML venues (e.g., RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR), including impactful first-author work in tactile sensing or dexterous manipulation
- Experience developing manipulation policies using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or foundation models for contact-rich tasks
- Demonstrated experience with sim-to-real transfer for tactile-enabled manipulation
- Familiarity with both learned and classical approaches to contact dynamics, including impedance and admittance control
- Experience with force and torque control, and with proprioceptive force estimation on torque- or current-controlled actuators
- Experience with robotics simulation stacks (e.g., Isaac, MuJoCo) and robot modeling (URDF)
- Experience with teleoperation and demonstration-collection pipelines for dexterous hands
- Familiarity with multi-finger or multi-contact gripper platforms

title: Software Dev Engineer II, SIFT
descriptionHtml:
Every day, the people closest to our customers and partners learn things that matter — in meetings, in deal rooms, in the field. For years most of that went nowhere useful: stuck in an inbox, a memory, a note no one opened again. We changed that. We built a product that captures those raw field inputs, automatically finds the patterns hiding across thousands of them, and uses AI to turn what used to be hours of manual report-writing into minutes — and it's now part of how a large, fast-growing community does its job every day.

That's the part that makes this interesting: it already works, at real scale, for a lot of people — and that raises the bar rather than lowering it. The hard problems now are the ones you only get to when something is genuinely in production and genuinely depended on. How do you keep quality high as usage climbs and the data gets messier? How do you make AI-generated output people trust instead of double-check? How do you extend a system people already rely on without breaking what they count on? This is applied AI in the critical path of real work — where "mostly right" isn't good enough and someone notices the moment it's off.

That's where you come in.

Here's the kind of thing you'd own and solve:

- Scale what's already working.
Take services that are live and heavily used and make them faster, sturdier, and ready for the next order of magnitude of users and data.

- Grow what the product can connect to.
Expand the set of tools and integrations the system exposes through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so the product can plug into more data sources and let AI assistants do more on a user's behalf — safely and reliably.

- Raise the quality bar on AI output.
Improve how the product turns messy, free-form input into trustworthy, structured, searchable records — with smarter summarization, tagging, and quality gating so strong output ships and weak output doesn't.

- Extend the product thoughtfully.
Add new capabilities and data sources to a system people already depend on, without disrupting the workflows they rely on every day.

- Make the trends sharper.
Improve how the product spots patterns across a huge body of individual stories, so people see what's emerging without digging for it.

- Let people talk to their data.
Build and refine the natural-language experiences that let someone ask for what they need — and get an answer built from real data, and only the data they're allowed to see.

- Keep it healthy.
Own the reliability and operations of what you build, dig into production issues when they happen, and raise the operational bar for the whole team.

What sets this apart: you're joining something that already succeeded — and the interesting work is everything that comes next. You get the best of both worlds: the real users, real feedback, and real impact of a product in heavy use, plus a wide-open set of hard problems around scaling it, deepening the AI, and taking it places it hasn't gone yet. You'll make architectural calls that matter, see your impact quickly because the people using it will tell you exactly what's working, and be expected to lift the engineers around you — mentoring, reviewing designs, and being someone who makes the whole team sharper, not just your own code.

We're looking for someone who's built and operated real backend systems at scale, is comfortable improving a live product without breaking it, and is genuinely excited about applying AI to a hard, valuable problem rather than chasing the buzz. Hands-on experience with generative AI and large language models is a strong prerequisite — and familiarity with Amazon Bedrock in particular will set you up to make an impact fast. If you like owning things end to end, caring about the person on the other side of the screen, and raising the bar on something people already love — you'll feel at home here.

Key job responsibilities
You'll own features end to end — from the user interface down to the backend services behind them — designing, building, and running them in production, where real people rely on them every day.

- Own whole features from the screen a user sees to the services and data underneath, making the design calls across the full stack and shipping each one to production.
- Build and scale the services that turn raw, free-form field input into structured, searchable, trustworthy records — keeping them fast and reliable as usage grows.
- Expand the tools and integrations the product exposes through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), connecting it to more data sources and letting AI assistants safely do more on a user's behalf.
- Wire large language models into the product and raise the quality bar on what they produce — sharper summarization, tagging, and quality gating so strong output ships and weak output doesn't.
- Build the natural-language experiences that let people ask for what they need and get answers grounded in real data — and only the data they're allowed to see.
- Write the design docs, run code reviews, debug the gnarly production issues, and mentor the engineers around you.

A day in the life
You're working where solid engineering meets applied AI — shipping real features people use the moment they go out.

You might push a feature you own from the screen a user sees down to the service behind it: write the code, get it reviewed, shepherd it through testing into production. A good chunk of your time goes into making the AI better — tuning how it drafts and summarizes, then checking the output against real examples to prove it improved. You'll join a short daily standup and review teammates' code.

Some days stretch further — debugging production issues, or prototyping an idea.

About the team
We build AI that changes how the sales field works. Our users are the people talking to AWS customers and partners every day — and our job is to turn the stories they gather into something they can use right away. We capture their input, surface the patterns across it, and draft the reports that used to eat hours of someone's week. You'll work shoulder to shoulder with engineers, product, and the field teams who depend on what we ship, to help shape where the product goes next. We move fast, listen to our users, and care about getting it right.

About AWS
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. title: EU QC In-stock specialist - 1 year FTC
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Quick Commerce (QC) delivers groceries and everyday essentials to customers in minutes from a network of local stores. To keep that promise, the right products have to be on our shelves at the right time. A large part of our range is supplied from Amazon's core fulfilment network into each QC store.

We are looking for a core in-stock specialist to own that flow every day. You will make sure the core selection is transferred in the right quantity, at the right time and to the right store, so customers find what they are looking for. You will manage day-to-day operations with the fulfilment centres, transport and store teams. You will be the first person to see a gap in availability and the person who closes it.

This is an operational role in a young and fast-growing network. Processes are still being built and volumes change quickly, especially around Peak and promotional events. You will need to act fast on data, raise issues early and keep stakeholders aligned. You will also help shape the mechanisms we use as we scale.

The applicable collective agreement for this role is CBA for employees of Logistics, Delivery and Shipping Sector. The position is classified at level 2 or above, depending on the candidate's skills, competences and experience.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the in-stock of the core selection across QC stores, tracking core VBI and store availability against target and acting on gaps every day.
- Plan and execute manual transfers from the core fulfilment centres to QC stores, setting quantities from demand forecasts, safety stock and store capacity.
- Schedule and manage CPTs with fulfilment centre and transport teams so transfers leave on time and arrive in line with store receiving windows.
- Run daily operations end to end: check transfer status, find stuck or short shipments, and fix issues with fulfilment centres, middle mile and store teams.
- Find the root causes of out-of-stocks, such as upstream availability, stock reserved for other channels, missed CPTs or receiving delays, and drive corrective actions with the owning teams.
- Review safety stock levels and resize deal and promotional ASINs per store based on forecast and sell-through, especially ahead of Peak events.
- Keep store space and capacity in mind when sending stock, so transfers do not create overstock or congestion in the store.
- Report weekly on in-stock, transfer performance and key issues, and escalate risks early with clear data and a proposed action.
- Contribute to new processes and tools as the network grows, for example automating manual transfers or launching direct fulfilment-centre-to-store injections.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in logistics, transportation, supply chain, import/export operations, or data entry/data administration
- Experience in an operational role, or experience working with data analytics and using these metrics to identify problems
- Experience communicating with a wide range of stakeholders, including colleagues and leadership

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with transfer planning, replenishment or transport scheduling in a fulfilment or store network.

Step 1: Congratulations! You successfully submitted your application!

Step 2: Amazon Recruiting will review your application and invite the most qualified candidate to complete a pre-employment assessment.

Step 3: If you meet the role qualifications, you will receive an invitation from Amazon Recruiting (do-not-reply@criteriacorp.com) to begin your Criteria assessment. You have 5 days to complete.

Step 4: Once you successfully meet the pre-employment assessment requirements, you will be invited to complete a video interview. Your video interview invitation will be from HireVue (interviews@hirevue.com) and you will have 7 days to record your interview.

Step 5: Your video interview will be reviewed by the Amazon Hiring Team and you will be notified of next steps via email within 5 business days.

- You will promote a safe working environment by following all safety procedures

descriptionHtml:
The Brazil Transportation Network Planning team is looking for a talented Senior Transportation Network Manager who will lead the planning and design of the end-to-end transportation network across all fronts — volume flows, middle-mile, and last-mile expansion. Communicate and drive long-term initiatives, actively removing bottlenecks and building scalable mechanisms, and partner with the science team to automate volume-flow planning.

Effectively influence stakeholders without direct authority, driving clear, precise, and regular communication through monthly and quarterly planning reviews.

Proactively identify gaps and opportunities in the planning process, benchmarking best practices from established markets to drive adoption in Brazil.

Contribute to mid- to long-term network design, process standardization, and the development of innovative transportation solutions.

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

- Experience in English-language communication skills, both written and verbal

Technical: Troubleshoot technical issues on various platforms ranging from Systems through Networking to Power/Mechanical

·
Project Management:

· Participate in and deliver on a number of high impact small to mid-scale projects
· Participate in internal team meetings at ADSIPL for metric analysis and project status updates
· Help build the world’s largest Cloud infrastructure in India

descriptionHtml:
Als Nachwuchsführungskraft wirst du in unserem 11-wöchigen internen Onboarding Programm auf deine neue Aufgabe als Führungskraft vorbereitet.
Nach dieser umfangreichen Einarbeitung übernimmst du Führungsverantwortung für dein eigenes Team und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Kunden Ihre Waren pünktlich und in guter Qualität erhalten. In dieser Position bist du wichtiger Teil unseres globalen Unternehmens und arbeitest Hand in Hand mit deinen Mitarbeitenden vor Ort. Zudem arbeitest du standortübergreifend an Themen wie Arbeitssicherheit, Prozessoptimierung, Nachhaltigkeit und technischem Fortschritt.


Key job responsibilities
Sicherstellung der Einhaltung der Arbeitssicherheitsvorschriften und des Umweltschutzes
Ableitung von Handlungsempfehlungen und konkreten Maßnahmen zur Prozessverbesserung auf Basis von Kennzahlen wie Arbeitssicherheit, Produktivität und Qualität
Leitung und Weiterbildung eines Teams (bis zu 100 Mitarbeitende)
Planung und Steuerung der innerbetrieblichen Prozesse
Teilnahme in übergeordneten Projekten zur Optimierung der Kundenzufriedenheit
Effektives Ressourcen- und Workflowmanagement
Zusammenarbeit mit den vor- und nachgelagerten Abteilungen vor Ort

A day in the life
Du arbeitest in einer unserer Schichten (Früh-, Spät- oder Nachtschicht). Dabei ist das Einhalten der Sicherheitsstandards an deinem gesamten Standort für dich höchste Priorität. Als Schichtleitung führst du routinemäßig Teammeetings durch und führst Feedbackgespräche mit deinen Mitarbeitenden und deinen Stakeholdern. Mit Hilfe von Datenauswertungen nimmst Du Einfluss auf die Produktivität und die Qualität deines Standortes. Als wichtiges Mitglied des Teams vor Ort arbeitest Du mit anderen Abteilungen, sowie externen Stakeholdern zusammen und sorgst dafür, dass wir die Anforderungen unserer Kundschaft, ebenso wie unsere eigenen Vorgaben jederzeit erfüllen. Durch die Analyse von Daten mit Führungskräften und die Besprechung der betrieblichen Vor- und Nachteile von technischen Verbesserungen mit den Fachabteilungen trägst du zu „best in class“ Lösungen bei.

About the team
Die Logistikabteilung bei Amazon (AMZL) ist für die „Last-Mile-Logistik“ zuständig – also die Auslieferung unserer Pakete in Partnerschaft mit Drittanbietern. Wir denken kreativ und realisieren Initiativen zur kontinuierlichen Verbesserung, um Millionen von physischen Produkten an unsere Kund:innen zu liefern. Unser Ziel ist es, das Liefererlebnis für unsere Kund:innen so reibungslos wie möglich zu machen und globale Lieferlösungen für unsere neuesten Angebote einzuführen, darunter Amazon Fresh, Prime Now und Amazon Restaurants.
Diese Tätigkeiten werden von zwei Mitarbeitergruppen ausgeführt. Unsere „internen“ Mitarbeitenden bereiten Millionen von Produkten auf den Versand an unsere Lieferteams vor. Unser Team ist menschenorientiert und hilfsbereit. Das ist besonders wichtig, weil viele unserer Mitarbeitenden in Nachtschichten arbeiten. Unser Fokus liegt vorwiegend auf dem operativen Betrieb. An den meisten unserer Standorte wird rund um die Uhr gearbeitet.
Unsere „Außendienst“-Mitarbeitenden arbeiten währenddessen mit Amazon Flex – einem Auftragnehmer-Netzwerk für die Lieferung. Jedes Jahr setzen wir neue Maßstäbe in puncto Kundenerlebnis und bieten neue, innovative Lieferdienste an. Wir suchen nach neuen Möglichkeiten, um branchenweite Logistikherausforderungen zu überwinden, sowie nach neuen Ideen, um unseren CO2-Fußabdruck zu reduzieren. Ein Fuhrpark innovativer Fahrzeuge (einschließlich E-Fahrzeugen) und modernste Technologie unterstützen uns dabei.

title: Senior Manager, DC Supply Chain, NA Supply Chain
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Senior Manager, DC Supply Chain Leader to lead the planning functions for our Distribution Center (DC) Supply Chain. This upstream inbound fulfillment network is critical to inventory placement and to how we receive product from our selling partners and vendors, and it plays a central role in getting the right inventory to the right place at the right time.

This is a leader-of-leaders role at the center of the network's performance — accountable for both the long-term strategy and the day-to-day tactical execution of the planning organization. As the network continues to grow and evolve, the right leader will shape how it plans, replenishes, and performs at scale.

This role demands strong ownership, a bias for action, the ability to Think Big, and the judgment to make high-quality decisions in ambiguous environments. You will be expected to earn trust across a broad set of cross-functional partners and to use data rigorously to justify and defend your decisions.

Key Responsibilities

Ambiguity & Strategic Leadership

- Lead teams where problems, opportunities, and strategies may not yet be defined, bringing structure to ambiguity.

- Apply significant domain expertise and high judgment to design the right team structure, mechanisms, and strategy to meet long-term business goals for the DC Supply Chain network.

- Independently balance short-term vs. long-term decisions, defining clear goals and objectives for the planning organization.

- Develop strategic goals for organizations and large customer/partner bases where the problem space is still emerging.

Scope of Influence

- Manage other managers across potentially multiple locations — operate as a **leader of leaders**.

- Influence team priorities and broader business strategy for the inbound network.

- Lead through teaching — educate the team on the larger picture, the long-term perspective, and the context behind business choices.

- Identify future leaders, provide them challenging opportunities, and facilitate their exposure to senior management.


Execution & Problem-Solving (Planning Focus)

- Provide strategic management and align planning teams to deliver for customers across S&OP, replenishment, and capacity planning.

- Proactively identify gaps and opportunities, delegate appropriately, and mitigate risks before they become roadblocks.

- Manage significantly complex problems and decisions, decomposing them into straightforward, executable solutions.

- Create scalable, long-term mechanisms, and establish mechanisms to evaluate scope and priority across projects.

- Escalate serious risks to leadership appropriately and in a timely manner.


Team & People Management

- Ensure the right people are in the right roles, and establish audit mechanisms to verify managers are actively managing careers.

- Proactively offer career-growth conversations and lead promotion processes when employees demonstrate next-level performance.

- Build a team that delivers successfully without your direct involvement, leveraging your role for escalations and removing blockers.


Communication & Impact

- Comfortable leading and earning trust with senior (L8/L10) stakeholders, with strong verbal and written communication skills.

- Be accountable for OP1/OP2 goals for the planning organization.

- Set the standard for process improvements and operational excellence across the network.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of team management experience
- 5+ years of supply chain experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization

Developer Experience organization owns the entire path from commit to satellite. This is a unique opportunity to offer this scope to platform engineers.
We will build a unified platform that empower Leo engineers to see their code affect satellite operations within days not weeks, months or a quarter.
