title: Software Development Manager, Leo AI Foundations, Amazon Leo AI Foundations
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's initiative to launch a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites to provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.

The Leo AI Foundations team builds the intelligence that will run Leo as an AI-native business. We combine applied science and engineering with Leo's domain expertise, own the shared AI foundation for the business, and lead work that spans teams and systems, so that progress in one part of Leo becomes a capability the whole business can use. Leo Lens is our command center for this AI network. It is pioneering agentic AI for diagnostics, reporting, troubleshooting and mitigating issues across our end-to-end network stack, and it automates workflows for mission operations, ecommerce and developer use cases. Through Lens, it is our vision that agents work as one system to keep the network secure and reliable, resolving failures before customers experience them, while Leo's teams keep authority over consequential decisions.

We are looking for a Software Development Manager to build and lead one of our engineering teams. You will own a roadmap in one of our tracks as we build the infrastructure for the AI that operates the network, from the agents themselves to the orchestration, knowledge access, evaluation and security controls that connect them. You will hire and grow a team of software engineers and applied scientists, partner with the domain teams that own satellites, gateways, customer terminals and network services, and deliver production systems where reliability, security and measurable impact are the bar.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Build, lead and develop a team of software engineers and applied scientists, from hiring and onboarding through career growth and performance.
- Own the team's roadmap and delivery: translate the AI Foundations charter into goals, milestones and launches, and report progress and risks to senior leadership.
- Lead the technical design and architecture of agentic AI systems for Leo, covering agent development, data integration and the platform services that connect agents to Leo's knowledge and systems.
- Bring deep, current knowledge of AI, including large language models, agent frameworks, retrieval and evaluation methods, and apply it to guide the team's technical choices and to raise the AI fluency of the partner teams you work with.
- Deliver production AI systems with the evaluation, access controls and operational readiness required to act on a live network, and expand agent autonomy only as evidence shows it is safe and effective.
- Own end-to-end delivery of complex, multi-team initiatives, including infrastructure migrations and platform improvements, with domain teams who retain ownership of their services.
- Set and uphold the engineering bar for the team: design and security reviews, testing, operational excellence and on-call health.
- Make prioritization calls in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment, balancing stability against new capabilities, and communicate trade-offs clearly.

A day in the life
No two days look the same, because you are building something that has not existed before. You will set the direction for your team and remove what stands in its way. You will sit with the engineers and scientists who own Leo's satellites, gateways, customer terminals and network services, and decide with them how your team's expertise in AI can unblock them or move them faster. You will meet the operators who keep the network healthy and turn their hardest problems into the next capability Lens delivers. You will hire and grow the people who build this, and represent your work to Leo's senior leadership.

About the team
We are an AI-native team of software engineers and applied scientists in Redmond, and we move fast. We use AI in how we build, not only in what we build, so a good idea can be a working experiment the same week and a production capability the next. We think beyond how things have been done, test our ideas against real problems, and keep only what proves itself. We ship lightning fast, and we hold a high bar for quality and production readiness while doing it.

- 7+ years of engineering experience
- 8+ years of leading the definition and development of multi tier web services experience
- 1+ years of providing technical leadership and project management for all aspects of the software development lifecycle experience
- 1+ years of developing large-scale, multi-tiered distributed software systems using Java, C#, or C++ experience
- 1+ years of developing large-scale, multi-tiered distributed software systems using service-oriented architecture experience
- 1+ years of developing large-scale, multi-tiered distributed software systems using distributed programming experience

- Experience delivering production systems built on large language models or ML, including evaluation, guardrails and cost management

title: Principal Applied Scientist, Ads Measurement Science
descriptionHtml:
The Measurement Science team in the Measurement, Ad Tech, and Data Science (MADS) organization of Amazon Ads serves a centralized role developing solutions for a multitude of performance measurement products. We create solutions which measure the comprehensive impact of their ad spend, including sales impacts both online and offline and across timescales, and provide actionable insights that enable our advertisers to optimize their media portfolios. We leverage a host of scientific technologies to accomplish this mission, including Generative AI, classical ML, Causal Inference, Natural Language Processing, and Computer Vision.

This Principal Applied Scientist leads the technical vision and execution for Amazon Advertising's performance measurement. Our measurement products and tools help customers understand the holistic impact of their spend on Amazon Ads and optimize their portfolios. This is a complex, multi-disciplinary scientific space spanning machine learning, causal inference, statistics and experimentation, natural language processing, and generative AI. As a GenAI-first organization, we build foundational and agentic models that power advertiser use cases across Ads, while empowering our Applied Scientists to directly build and ship products.

You will guide a team of scientists with expertise across different domains to come together and innovate on some of the hardest problems in advertising, made more challenging by evolving privacy regulations and technological changes. In measuring the comprehensive impact of advertising, key challenges you will tackle include capturing impact: 1) both for identified and increasingly unidentified web traffic in light of an evolving global privacy landscape; 2) for outcomes across retailers, including both within and beyond Amazon; and 3) for both short- and long-term impacts of advertising.


Key job responsibilities
* Driving the scientific vision of the teams in your organization and you advise and influence its technical leadership on performance measurement models and products.
* Identifying, tackling, and proposing innovative solutions to intrinsically hard, previously unsolved problems. You solve problems pragmatically, applying judgment and experience to balance trade-offs between competing interests.
* Bringing clarity to complex problems, probing assumptions, illuminating pitfalls, fostering shared understanding, and guiding towards effective solutions.
* Serving and being recognized by internal and external peers as a thought leader in modeled measurement in Ads. You will engage routinely with the broader scientific community, e.g. as a reviewer, program committee member, workshop organizer, or chair at peer-reviewed internal/external conferences.
* Leading by example, with your papers, analyses, and code setting the standard in your organization for scientific engineering excellence.
* Leading science and design reviews, aligning teams across your organization around coherent algorithmic strategies.
* Influencing your team’s science and business strategy by driving one or more team roadmaps contributing to the organization’s roadmap and taking responsibility for some organizational goals. You drive multiple new product features from inception to production launch.
* Guiding the career development of others, actively mentoring and educating the larger applied science community on trends, technologies, and best practices. You drive the documentation of scientific innovation. You attract bar-raising talent from academia and industry.
* Staying abreast of academic and industry trends, knowing the state of the art, and building on top of existing solutions instead of reinventing when possible.

About the team
We are a team of scientists across Applied, Research, Data Science and Economist disciplines. You will work with colleagues with deep expertise in ML, NLP, CV, Gen AI, and Causal Inference with a diverse range of backgrounds. We partner closely with top-notch engineers, product managers, sales leaders, and other scientists with expertise in the ads industry and on building scalable modeling and software solutions.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of hands-on work in predictive modeling and analysis experience
- PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related technical field
- Experience working in predictive modeling and analysis
- Experience distilling informal customer requirements into problem definitions, dealing with ambiguity and competing objectives
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience with leading experienced scientists as well as having a record of developing junior members from academia or industry to a career track in a business environment

Preferred qualifications

- 10+ years of relevant work in industry or academia experience
- Knowledge of problem solving, algorithm design and complexity analysis
- Experience creating novel algorithms and advancing the state of the art

- Deep expertise in ad tech and/or ad measurement problems

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Australia helps Australian businesses of every size reach millions of customers and grow their business. The AU 3P Seller Services team recruits local businesses to sell in the Amazon.com.au store and supports their success and growth. Much of that growth is delivered through Account Managers (AMs), who manage seller portfolios, solve problems for sellers and help them adopt the programs that grow their business. Our vision is for every AM to spend their time on the work that moves sellers forward, backed by tools that do the rest.

The AM Tools Product team builds and launches the products AMs use every day: seller insights, portfolio prioritisation, escalation tracking, reporting and AI assistants. We work with Amazon's global seller services, tech and AI teams to bring the right capabilities to Australian AMs, and we build our own where local needs call for it. As AI becomes central to how AMs work, we are building AI-powered tools that automate routine work, surface the next best action for each seller, and let one AM support more sellers with more impact.

We are looking for a Product Manager to own AM tools end to end, from discovery through launch, adoption and measured impact. The ideal candidate knows how AMs actually spend their day, spots where time is lost, studies working models to find patterns, and designs tools that remove that friction. They earn trust with AMs and their leaders, drive adoption through training, enablement and change management, and are accountable for whether a tool changes how the team works and what sellers achieve. They work across engineering, data science, BI, UX, and AM and operations leadership in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.

You will own a product area end to end and see its impact directly in how AMs work and how sellers grow. You will build hands-on experience with GenAI and agentic products, from model evaluation to responsible AI practices, alongside data scientists and ML engineers. You will work with senior leaders in AU 3P and with global seller services and AI teams, which builds your influence and network across Amazon. Amazon also supports your development through product management training, mentoring from senior PMs, and room to take on a larger scope as the AM tools portfolio grows.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and own the AM tools strategy and roadmap across seller segments and the AM workflow, prioritising the investments that return the most AM time and seller growth.
- Build and launch AI-powered tools with partner teams, including GenAI assistants, automated seller insights and agentic workflows. Write clear requirements that balance technical feasibility, user needs, business impact and responsible AI standards.
- Drive adoption and change management after launch: run pilots and staged rollouts, design training and champion programs, retire redundant tools, and align AM leadership on new ways of working.
- Measure the impact of every tool through adoption, AM time saved, seller coverage and seller success, and report results through regular business reviews.
- Partner with global AM tooling, seller services and AI teams to reuse existing solutions, shape their roadmaps for Australian needs, and manage leadership communication on solution reviews and impact.

A day in the life
About a third of your time goes to collaboration: shadowing AMs, running discovery sessions, and working through requirements and trade-offs with partner teams. Around a quarter is deep focus, where you write PRFAQs and requirements, analyse adoption and productivity data, and plan launches. Another quarter goes to meetings with AM leaders and global partner teams: roadmap reviews, launch readiness and business reviews. You spend the rest in the field with users, running pilots, training sessions and feedback loops, and checking that each tool works in the AM's real day.

About the team
Our team is part of Amazon's AU 3P Seller Services organization. We build and maintain the tools that hundreds of Account Managers rely on every day to support thousands of Australian 3P sellers. We partner closely with Amazon's global seller services, AI, and engineering teams, as well as local operations and AM leadership. Our focus is on making AMs more effective through better tooling and AI-powered automation, so that every Australian seller gets the hands-on support they need to grow their business on Amazon.

title: Trust and Privacy TPM, Devices & Services Trust, Privacy, and Accessibility
descriptionHtml:
Devices & Services Trust, Privacy and Accessibility (TPA) is responsible for maintaining and raising the trust bar for Amazon customers across 30+ Devices and Services. We offer horizontal services for builders to ensure trust, privacy, and accessibility is built into our products and services. We also build customer-facing capabilities that provide customers with control and transparency while reducing trust risks, and enable partner teams to innovate with appropriate guardrails for privacy, safety and appropriateness, creative content, fairness, veracity, security, and accessibility.

As we expand our scope into trust incident response and crisis management, we are growing the team to address trust risks across our devices and services portfolio. The TPA team is seeking a Technical Program Manager to join our Trust Incident & Crisis Management function. In this role, you will manage incident response for high-severity, trust-impacting events, from intake through containment, mitigation, and closure, operating the mechanisms, playbooks, and metrics that keep this an always-on operation. You will act as incident manager during active events, drive escalations with urgency, keep stakeholders aligned, and write clear briefs for senior leadership. This is a high-impact, high-visibility position that directly protects customer trust across our products and services, and partners with our India-based incident leads to sustain continuous, cross-time-zone (follow-the-sun) coverage.

A successful candidate will have a strong background driving cross-functional programs, solid program-management, technical problem-solving, and communication skills, and be comfortable operating at a technical level with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You should understand systems and trade-offs well enough to ask the right questions and support sound decisions, derive insights from complex data, write clear business documents, and hold partner teams accountable to shared commitments through to closure. The ability to stay detail-oriented and decisive under pressure will be critical to success in this role.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end response for assigned trust-impacting incidents by defining scope and success criteria, proactively identifying and mitigating risks across dependent teams, and driving each case to closure within SLA.
- Set up incident rooms for high-severity events; triage, classify, escalate, and coordinate response under pressure using established severity matrices.
- Partner with engineering and product stakeholders to understand system architecture, data flows, and design trade-offs, ensuring remediation meets scalability, performance, and operational standards.
- Drive root-cause analysis and post-mortems (correction-of-error), track corrective and preventative actions across Engineering and Product through to closure, and prepare incident narratives, escalation briefs, and status updates for leadership.
- Evaluate opportunities to apply generative artificial intelligence tools and process improvements to streamline detection and triage workflows, while mentoring peers and contributing to team hiring efforts.

A day in the life
As a Technical Program Manager on the Trust Incident & Crisis Management team, you will work on high-impact, high-visibility programs that directly protect our customers. You start your day triaging newly reported issues across trust surfaces and picking up open incidents and corrective actions. During an active event you step into the incident-manager role: classify severity, coordinate the response, assign clear ownership for each action, and keep every item moving to closure within SLA. Between events you run post-incident reviews, keep playbooks and dashboards current, and partner with Engineering and Product to embed trust-by-design practices upstream. You collaborate across trust, privacy, accessibility, security, engineering, legal, and product teams to drive these programs from intake to resolution.

About the team
Our Trust Incident & Crisis Management function sits within Devices & Services Trust, Privacy and Accessibility (TPA), building the programs and services at Amazon scale that grow customer trust, create mechanisms to meet evolving regulatory objectives, and ensure our partners can fulfill their trust obligations without disruption. We run a single, consistent, always-on operating model for high-severity, trust-impacting events: detection, coordination, containment, and crisis response. This is a newly expanded area of investment, so it is a great time to join and help shape how we build out this capability. We value collaboration, continuous learning, and operational rigor, and we support new members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
- 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 2+ years of software development experience
- 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience with roadmap strategy and definition

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- Experience in Incident Management, Threat Management, Corporate Investigations, Law Enforcement, Security Operations, Crisis Management or a related field
- Experience working effectively across cross-functional teams and partnering well with people at all levels within an organization
- Experience in root cause analysis and error correction, identifying changes to procedures and systems to implement long-term fixes and avoid repeating issues
- Experience in written and verbal communication with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to executives and non-technical leaders

title: Lead Mechanical Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services is seeking a Lead Mechanical Engineer to lead the mechanical architecture of the 5-10 MW SST, including enclosure/rack architecture, interfaces, IP protection, vibration and seismic qualification.

As a Lead Mechanical Engineer you will define enclosure/rack architecture, interfaces, IP rating and serviceability for the 5–10 MW system from an open requirement space. You will own structural, thermal, environmental (vibration/seismic) and manufacturability constraints at system scale, plus escalations. You will chair mechanical reviews, coordinate suppliers/manufacturing, mentor designers, and align interfaces with thermal, electrical and MV/HV.

About AIS
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
Mechanical architecture:
- Define the mechanical architecture for the 5–10 MW system and its major assemblies.
- Develop rack/enclosure concepts compatible with high-power electronics and liquid cooling.
- Define mechanical interfaces with power, PCB, magnetics, cooling and electrical integration.

Environmental requirements:
- Address IP-rating requirements.
- Define and assess vibration and seismic qualification requirements.
- Consider serviceability, accessibility and maintainability in the mechanical design.

Design leadership:
- Lead mechanical design reviews.
- Coordinate suppliers and manufacturing for prototype and production parts.
- Support mechanical qualification, prototype builds and system integration.

SST System Alignment"
- Design against the system specification environmental envelope where applicable: NEMA 3R outdoor rating, -30°C to 40°C operating range, C5 corrosion class, 95% RH non-condensing, ≤1000 m site elevation and defined transport/seismic loads.
- Account for the system physical envelope guidance and serviceability/transport constraints while developing the 5–10 MW platform.



A day in the life
As a Lead Mechanical Engineer, you'll focus on developing mechanical architecture for our 5-10 MW power systems, working with cutting-edge liquid cooling and high-power electronics integration. Your day might include chairing mechanical design reviews where you evaluate structural and thermal concepts, coordinating with suppliers on prototype development, or mentoring junior designers through complex design challenges. You'll balance strategic architecture decisions with hands-on problem-solving—defining how components interface with electrical, thermal, and manufacturing teams. You'll also assess environmental requirements like vibration and seismic qualification, ensuring our systems operate reliably across diverse global locations from coastal to high-altitude environments.

About the team
We are AWS Infrastructure Services—the team that keeps the cloud running for millions of customers worldwide. We design, plan, deliver, and operate all AWS global infrastructure, managing thousands of variables across the supply chain to ensure continuous innovation and reliability. Our team is composed of collaborative engineers who thrive in solving complex, interconnected problems. We're building the next generation of power systems, and we're looking for someone who shares our commitment to safety, scalability, and operational excellence. You'll work alongside thermal engineers, electrical specialists, and manufacturing partners, contributing to a shared vision of more efficient, reliable infrastructure. Our customers depend on us, and we depend on talented people like you to help shape the future of cloud infrastructure.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to celebrate our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and diversity conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We have a career path for you no matter what stage you’re in when you start here. We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related experience.
- Demonstrated understanding of IP rating, vibration and seismic qualification.
- Experience integrating high-power electronics and thermal-management systems.
- Experience documenting design decisions, assumptions, trade-offs, risks and technical specifications.
- Experience using engineering analysis and measured evidence to drive decisions.
- Experience demonstrating maintaining a strong focus on safety, reliability, serviceability and scalable deployment.

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering.
- 5+ years leading mechanical design for power/electrical equipment or comparable high-power enclosures.
- Strong mechanical-engineering experience in complex industrial equipment.
- Experience with SolidWorks and/or CATIA V5.
- Demonstrated working effectively with adjacent engineering disciplines and contribute to full A-to-Z product ownership.
- Demonstrated operating effectively in a greenfield environment where standards and reference designs may require interpretation and adaptation.

title: Procurement Category Manager, OneMHS Procurement & Supply Chain
descriptionHtml:
Amazon installs a significant quantity of new buildings every year. The historical model has been to allow each integrator to use their own equipment, controls, subsystems, and methodologies. While that has allowed Amazon to be successful to this point, the variability between buildings has proven difficult to support and scale. One MHS’ charge is to build partnerships to focus on consistency and scalability across our network of the future. We will be partnering with key suppliers to help them scale up their manufacturing capabilities to keep up with our needs, as well as refining their designs to drive innovation and operational uptime and better meet the specific needs of Amazon’s operational environment. In partnership with WWDE, OMHS will challenge the status quo on our Gen14 AR sortables building by focusing on critical equipment, controls, and system implementation methods. We are seeking a Procurement Category Manager (PCM) to join our One-MHS team & to partner with internal business owners and key stakeholders across One-MHS & partner organizations, to drive procurement and operational value for these MHE systems. This role leads the development and execution of capital sourcing strategies for equipment, components that are part of the overall MHE systems. Our PCM drive efficiencies in procurement strategy and commercial pricing, enable engineering efficiencies through effective partnership with Amazon’s design teams, and support Amazon’s long-term business interests through partnership within One-MHS teams as well as other teams like GPO, Capital Planning, Project Management Organization (PMO), Worldwide Design Engineering (WWDE), Finance, Global Engineering Services (GES) Operations Engineering (Ops Eng.), and Reliability and Maintenance Engineering (RME).
This role will involve developing and executing category sourcing strategies, delivering savings, and improving productivity across the category. The ideal candidate will be a self-starter, a creative critical thinker, a builder who likes to build from scratch and a motivated learner with strong communication skills.


Key job responsibilities
• Develop and implement category sourcing strategies for equipment & components that form the overall MHE system or sub-systems, ensuring alignment with One-MHS goals and objectives.
• Lead cross-functional sourcing events, negotiate with suppliers, and execute contracts to optimize Amazon’s competitive position for the procured equipment.
• Manage internal and external relationships with key stakeholders, including suppliers, business units, and other procurement teams.
• Collaborate with global and local teams to deploy and manage the implementation of defined strategies.
• Influence suppliers’ roadmaps, design, processes, technology decisions, and strategies to align with Amazon’s procurement goals.
• Lead complex and cross-functional projects to drive productivity and innovation within the category.
• Monitor market trends, competitor activities, and industry best practices to inform category strategies and decision-making.
• Develop and maintain category-specific metrics and reporting to track performance, savings, and supplier compliance.

Basic qualifications

title: Senior Modem Engineer, Satellite Communication
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.

In this role you will:
. Engage with modem system teams to translate system-level requirements into hardware specifications and RTL implementation.
· Collaborate with system architects on SoC subsystem integration, including IP block configuration, instantiation, and interface validation.
· Support synthesis, static timing analysis (STA), and timing closure activities to meet performance and power targets.
· Contribute to low-power design implementation and verification, including power domain definition and UPF/CPF development.
· Work with verification, physical design, and firmware teams to ensure design quality and first-time-right silicon.
· Develop and maintain comprehensive gate-level simulation test plans for verifying ASIC functionality and timing. Analyze simulation results, identify and debug logic errors, and propose solutions.
. Work closely with design and verification engineers to validate fixes and ensure design closure.
· Develop AI-assisted Design Automation/Debug skills for various aspects of SoC development.

Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

. Define, configure and integration SoC Subsystems
. Own one or more Modem IP blocks.

. Define and develop any necessary support logic
. Configure, instantiate and integrate 3rd party IP blocks

. Perform initial synthesis & timing analysis
. Assist verification team in unit verification including test plan development
. Assist with debug and bring-up


About the team
Be part of Leo's sub-team responsible for defining and implementing the digital chip SOCs for communications via Low Earth Orbit satellites and Amazon gateways. This is a unique opportunity to define a state-of-the-art wireless solution with few legacy constraints. The team works with customer requirements and wireless system teams to define modems, high-speed interfaces, embedded processors, and custom solutions in latest CMOS generation technologies.

- 7+ years of experience in digital design, preferably in SoC design and implementation.
- Experience with Modem SoC design and development.

Preferred qualifications

- 7+ years of digital design in communication systems experience
- Master's or Ph.D degree in Electrical / Communications Engineering.
- Deep understanding of modem SoC architecture, including PHY/MAC subsystems and system-level integration.

title: Controls Coordinator, Asia-Pacific Controls Deployment & Service (APAC CDS)
descriptionHtml:
Are you someone who looks at a process and immediately sees what could be automated, documented better, or removed entirely? The Program Management and Coordination team within AWS Infrastructure Services is growing to support an expanding portfolio of data centre sites across Asia-Pacific, and we are looking for a Controls Coordinator to own the transactional backbone of controls delivery across APAC. You will manage every work order, change order, purchase request, purchase order, and capital appropriation request end to end against published SLAs, partnering with Controls Engineers, Finance, Legal, and Procurement to turn engineering decisions into committed spend.

The timing matters. The team is part-way through automating its own transactional work, so you will help design that tooling rather than inherit it finished. Vendor management is also becoming a defined programme rather than something each coordinator handles independently, giving you a clear area to own from the start. No data centre experience is needed. What matters is what you do with a process once you hold it: writing the run book a new joiner can follow without asking, building the report that answers the question before it gets asked, and automating the parts that should never have been manual.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage every work order, change order, purchase request, purchase order, and capital appropriation request end to end, tracking each against its published SLA and escalating exceptions early with a recommendation attached.
- Coordinate with Controls Engineers, Finance, Legal, and Procurement across APAC to land commitments that carry real money, including support for annual and mid-year operating plans.
- Design and maintain run books and process documentation so that workflows survive your absence and can be followed by any team member without additional guidance.
- Build reporting and automation that removes routine processing from people, using AI tools where they add value, and measure the before-and-after impact of every improvement you deliver.
- Own the vendor management programme for your region, defining consistent processes and partnering with global counterparts across a follow-the-sun operating model.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with your queue: the requests are yours from day one, and so are the blockers behind them. You might spend the first hour clearing purchase orders through their approval chain, then shift to refining an automation that shaves a manual step off the change-order workflow. After a standup with your Controls Engineering partners, you review an open vendor issue with Procurement and draft the escalation note. Later you pull together the data for a business review that senior leadership will read directly. Between tasks you are testing a new AI-driven dashboard the team is building in-house. By the end of the day you have moved work forward, removed a friction point, and documented what you changed so the next person does not have to ask.

About the team
The Program Management and Coordination team is the governance group within AWS Infrastructure Services that owns the planning cycles, goals, business reviews, and mechanisms the APAC region runs on. This is where process gets designed rather than requested. The team is eight people today, spread across Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney, and Melbourne, and everyone sits within the same Tech Ops Engineering job family — meaning the step from coordinator to programme manager is a genuine progression on a single ladder.

Our closest partners are the Controls Engineers running deployments, projects, service, and colocation across APAC, along with Finance, Legal, and Procurement on every commitment that carries money. We also collaborate with our counterparts in the Americas and EMEA through a global follow-the-sun model, so a process you improve once is improved everywhere we operate.

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our department, Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD), sponsors leadership programs that support the growth and development of builders across the organization. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events build stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation draws on the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Basic qualifications

- Experience producing written documentation, processes or reports that other people rely on without needing you to explain them
- Experience using generative AI tools in daily work, getting useful results from them on real tasks rather than experimenting
- Experience owning a queue or pipeline of transactional work against a deadline or a service level

Preferred qualifications

- Experience improving or standardising a process, with a measured before and after
- Experience working with data: extracting it, reconciling it and reporting on it, in spreadsheets, SQL or a business intelligence tool
- Experience building automation, whether with AI agents, workflow tools, low code platforms or scripts
- Experience in program or project management, including cross-functional delivery
- Experience reading and querying commercial contracts, purchase orders or invoices

title: Sr. Manager, Global SMB Ads Marketing
descriptionHtml:
The Senior Manager, SMB Global Performance Marketing leads the worldwide first-party (1P) channel marketing team and content strategy for Amazon Ads' Small and Medium Business (SMB) segment. This leader owns two critical pillars: 1) Owned and operated ("1P") marketing channels (email, in-portal nudges across Seller/Vendor Central, Ad Console...), and 2) Click Credit promotions strategy and execution. The role spans demand programs (Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Brand Stores, and others), as well as vertical programs for Amazon Business and Authors.

Rooted in a deep understanding of SMB advertiser needs, this leader acts as the strategic bridge between customers and the broader Ads organization—translating pain points, behaviors, and performance signals into lifecycle marketing strategies that drive long-term growth. By combining customer and performance insights with business objectives, this role shapes messaging, influences product direction, and ensures marketing efforts align to advertiser success across their lifecycle. Success is measured through business impact: advertiser activation, retention, and sustained revenue growth.

As the team evolves toward an AI-enabled operating model in 2027, this leader will guide the transition from static campaign execution to continuous iteration—where Marketing Demand Automation (DMA) anchors end-to-end advertiser journeys, and marketers shift from hands-on execution to active system stewardship. This includes guiding strategy, defining business requirements, interpreting advertiser sentiment, and continuously calibrating outcomes based on customer satisfaction, engagement, and business impact.

Key job responsibilities
1. Owned and Operated ("1P") Marketing Channels
- Define and execute the worldwide 1P channel marketing strategy across email and in-portal nudges, driving reach, engagement, and attributed revenue at scale.
- Own end-to-end advertiser growth domains—acquisition, optimization, growth, and retention—defining problem statements, shaping strategy, and owning performance outcomes across the full advertiser lifecycle.
- Design customer-centric, experience-led marketing around cohesive end-to-end advertiser journeys.
- In partnership with decision science and mar-tech, define content frameworks, value propositions, and modular messaging that power 1:1 personalized experiences at scale.
- Own demand generation and performance, managing trade-offs between volume, quality, and Return on Investment (ROI) to maximize total business impact.
- Drive deep dive analysis and continuous experimentation.
- Lead the transition toward Marketing Demand Automation as the anchor of the operating model, shaping increasingly precise inputs and content frameworks to unlock scaled variation, personalization, and performance over time.

2. Click Credit Promotions
- Own the worldwide promotions strategy, including offer design, experimentation, and performance measurement, operating promotions as a key lever within Marketing Demand Automation journeys.
- Define and optimize promotional offer structures that incentivize advertisers to take actions supporting long-term changed behaviors.
- Drive continuous experimentation on promotional targeting, timing, and value to maximize incremental revenue and advertiser activation while managing ROI trade-offs.
- Converge promotions into a unified system across targeting, journeys, and messaging strategy, ensuring promotional offers are integrated within lifecycle marketing rather than operating as standalone tactics.

3. Strategic Leadership and Team Development
- Lead and develop a high-performing team of marketers operating as single-threaded owners across their respective domains.
- Guide the team's evolution from content creation to curation, system design, and business impact as AI scales execution.
- Serve as the strategic bridge between SMB advertisers and the broader Ads organization.

15+ years of work experience, 5+ years of management experience of international teams in a fast moving environment, MBA

Preferred qualifications

Experience developing cross-functional relationships with product, consumer research and marketing teams to develop strategy and consumer insights that drive compelling creative executions
Experience leading creative development of innovative creative from concept to delivery

title: Risk Manager II, Continuous Improvement, Relay Product Excellence
descriptionHtml:
Want to own how an organization gets better at what it does? Relay Product Excellence (RPE) protects Customers, Carriers, Drivers, and Amazon globally through fast-paced investigation and analytics, and we need an owner for the Continuous Improvement pillar within our Strategic Programs and Organizational eXcellence (SPOX) team. This is hands-on process work: you'll map how work actually flows today, standardize it into clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and build the documentation that makes the right way the easy way.

In this role, you'll own the Continuous Improvement pillar end to end, help shape the direction for how SPOX raises quality, consistency, and efficiency across a growing portfolio of risk and investigation initiatives. You'll build the mechanisms that find process gaps, size the opportunity, and drive improvements to closure, then institutionalize them so gains stick. You'll define what "good" looks like for execution standards and operating rhythms, and you'll measure whether the organization is actually getting better over time.

Because improvements are driven across risk operations, you'll need to be versed in risk or investigations, enough to read the work, spot where the real opportunities are, and partner credibly with the functional subject matter experts across RPE who run it. You'll partner closely with the Program Delivery, Special Programs, and Workforce Intelligence & Strategic Planning pillars to embed continuous improvement into how work gets delivered day to day. The ideal candidate brings strong communication skills, attention to detail, and a data-driven mindset, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders, earn trust across partner teams, and drive change independently in a fast-paced environment. The ideal candidate is someone who genuinely enjoys the craft of process mapping, standardization, and documentation.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the Continuous Improvement pillar within SPOX end to end, partnering with SPOX leader to set its roadmap, define its mechanisms, and measure its impact on quality, consistency, and efficiency across the organization.

- Identify process gaps and improvement opportunities, size them with data, and drive them to closure, then institutionalize the changes so gains are sustained.

- Map current-state processes end to end, standardize them into clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and build and maintain the documentation (process maps, runbooks, work instructions) that keeps execution consistent and audit-ready across the organization.

- Apply working knowledge of risk or investigations to identify where the biggest improvement opportunities sit, and partner effectively with functional subject matter experts across RPE to drive continuous improvement across risk operations.

- Define and raise execution standards for how programs are delivered, embedding continuous improvement into mechanisms within the operating rhythm (Weekly Business Reviews (WBRs) and Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs)) and OP planning cycle.

- Partner with the Program Delivery and Special Programs pillars under SPOX to translate improvement opportunities into delivered change across cross-functional initiatives with org-wide impact.

- Influence stakeholders through data-driven insights, written narratives, and clear recommendations.

- Operate with high integrity and discretion, handling sensitive data in compliance with Amazon's data classification and privacy policies.

A day in the life
In this role, you'll work through ambiguity regularly, reviewing program health metrics, spotting where the organization can get better, and prioritizing the improvements that matter most. While you own the strategy and roadmap for the pillar, the core of your week at the working level is hands-on process work: sitting with SMEs to map how a process actually works, turning that into a standardized SOP, and documenting it so it holds up over time. You'll drive alignment across RPE teams through influence, not authority, translating data into clear narratives for stakeholders to reach alignment and buy-in.

About the team
Middle Mile Transportation Technology moves millions of packages across Amazon's network daily, and Relay Product Excellence (RPE) ensures those systems stay protected. We sit at the intersection of product and operations, building programs that close gaps where automation hasn't yet reached. Our program managers, analysts, and investigators deliver rapid-cycle investigation and analytics that safeguard Customers, Carriers, Drivers, and Amazon globally.

Within RPE, the Strategic Programs and Organizational eXcellence (SPOX) team is the connective tissue, spanning Program Delivery, Escalations, Team Growth, Continuous Improvement, and Special Programs. SPOX owns the program management frameworks, milestone governance, execution methodology, and operating rhythms that give teams structure to move fast. We don't support delivery; we set the standard.

- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of compliance program management, legal, governance, audit, risk/loss prevention, or equivalent experience
- Experience establishing successful partnerships with internal and external teams to execute tactical initiatives or equivalent
- Experience in creating process improvements with automation and analysis
- Experience with data analysis tools such as Excel, Pivot Tables, macros, SQL, visualization tools - Tableau, Quicksight, etc.
- Experience owning program or process improvement end to end and communicating results to stakeholders
- Experience creating Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), process maps, and process documentation

Preferred qualifications

- Experience owning or leading a continuous improvement function, program, or methodology (for example Lean, Six Sigma, or Kaizen)

Build AI agents that turn customer intent into action, and help shape how software is built at Amazon.

As a Senior Manager of Software Development in Devices Software and Services, you will build and develop teams delivering intelligent experiences across mobile, web, and connected devices. title: FinOps Manager - AP, Accounts Payable Operations team
descriptionHtml:
FinOps Manager – Accounts Payable
Amazon Financial Operations | Level 5 | Full-Time | US Shift


Every payment Amazon makes to a supplier starts with a promise - and the Accounts Payable Operations team is the engine that keeps that promise, at massive scale, across dozens of subsidiaries and global marketplaces. As a FinOps Manager – AP, you’ll lead a core US-shift team responsible for the full invoice lifecycle - from ingestion through successful payment execution - ensuring that tens of thousands of vendors worldwide are paid accurately and on time.

This is a high-visibility leadership role at the intersection of operational excellence and financial transformation. You’ll own the transition of multiple subsidiary AP processes into a centralized operating model, build the playbooks that scale our operations for Amazon’s continued expansion, and drive automation initiatives that directly reduce manual touchpoints and cost-per-transaction. If you’re energized by building teams, simplifying complexity, and delivering measurable outcomes in a fast-moving environment - this role was made for you.

Role Overview

The FinOps Manager – Accounts Payable will lead a team supporting core US-shift AP operations and play a critical role in ensuring financial operations are scalable, efficient, and prepared for continued business growth.

The role will have end-to-end ownership of the Accounts Payable process, from invoice ingestion through invoice processing, exception/hold resolution, and successful payment execution. The manager will work closely with upstream and downstream teams across Finance, Procurement, Technology, and business functions to ensure timely and accurate processing and payments.

The role will also be responsible for transitioning and stabilizing AP processes for multiple subsidiaries. This includes building and developing high-performing teams, managing operational performance, establishing priorities, driving process improvements, and ensuring compliance with global policies, controls, and service-level commitments.
The successful candidate will be a strong people leader and operational owner with a passion for process innovation, automation, controllership, and customer/vendor experience. The candidate should be comfortable operating in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and independently solving complex and ambiguous business problems.


Basic Qualifications

1. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree with 10+ years of post-qualification experience in Accounts Payable, Finance Operations, Shared Services, or a related field.

2. 5+ years of project management and people management experience, including experience leading cross-functional initiatives with technical and non-technical teams.

3. Strong understanding of Accounts Payable operations and end-to-end financial processes.

4. Demonstrated ability to manage large-scale operations, transitions, and process changes.

5. Strong customer focus with experience managing internal and external stakeholders.

6. Demonstrated ability to operate independently and make sound decisions in ambiguous situations.

7. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

8. Results-oriented mindset with a demonstrated ability to delive
r against challenging goals.

9. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

10. Ability and willingness to work in flexible/night shifts, weekends, and holidays based on business requirements.




Preferred Qualifications

1. 4+ years of experience driving continuous improvement initiatives that improved controllership, operational efficiency, or scalability with measurable results.

2. 4+ years of experience identifying incomplete or inaccurate data, performing root-cause analysis, and developing and implementing escalation/corrective-action plans.

3. 4+ years of experience mentoring and developing junior finance, operations, or business team members.

4. Experience managing global or multi-geography Accounts Payable operations.

5. Experience with process transitions, migrations, or integration of new subsidiaries.

6. Experience working with automation, workflow, self-service, or finance technology solutions.

7. Experience developing operational metrics and using data to drive business decisions.




Key job responsibilities
1. Lead, manage, and develop a team of AP Specialists and Operations Managers supporting end-to-end Accounts Payable operations.

2. Own day-to-day operational performance and ensure accuracy, timeliness, productivity, quality, and SLA adherence.

3. Successfully lead the transition of multiple subsidiary AP processes into the operations team, ensuring smooth migration, stabilization, and business continuity.

4. Manage hiring, onboarding, training, coaching, performance management, and career development for team members.

5. Establish team priorities, allocate workload effectively, and ensure appropriate resource planning based on business requirements and volume forecasts.

6. Drive systems, process, and operational improvements to enable on-time and accurate vendor payments.

7. Identify opportunities to eliminate manual processes through automation, standardization, and self-service solutions.

8. Own and drive adherence to AP policies, procedures, and controls while ensuring consistency across global entities.

9. Act as a senior escalation point for complex vendor, customer, payment, invoice, and operational issues, ensuring timely resolution and appropriate stakeholder communication.

10. Proactively identify recurring issues, analyze service trends, perform root-cause analysis, and implement corrective and preventive actions.

11. Develop, maintain, and monitor operational metrics and dashboards covering SLA performance, payment timeliness, productivity, quality, defects, backlog, cost, and customer/vendor experience.

12. Drive cost optimization initiatives and identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and scalability.

13. Partner with Finance leadership to forecast future headcount requirements based on business growth, transaction volumes, country expansion, and operational demand.

14. Expand self-service capabilities and digital solutions to improve the vendor experience while reducing manual intervention.

15. Provide regular weekly and monthly business reviews, performance updates, and operational insights to Director- and VP-level Finance stakeholders.

16. Develop, implement, and maintain effective internal controls across AP processes.

17. Partner with Internal Audit, controllership, compliance, and finance teams to address control gaps and audit requirements.

18. Lead cross-functional technology, systems, and process-improvement initiatives involving Finance, Procurement, Operations, and technical teams.

20. Work effectively with stakeholders across multiple geographies and time zones, including support for US business hours, flexible/night shifts, weekends, and holidays based on business requirements.

21. Ensure operational readiness for new business launches, subsidiary transitions, process changes, and organizational growth.


How you’ll spend your time: Expect roughly 40% leading and coaching your team, 25% on cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder communication, 20% on process improvement and automation projects, and 15% on deep-focus analysis (metrics, controls, forecasting).


People Leadership

The manager will be responsible for building and maintaining a high-performing AP organization by:

a) Hiring and developing strong finance and operations talent.
b) Establishing clear performance expectations and measurable goals.
c) Conducting regular performance reviews and providing actionable feedback.
d) Identifying development opportunities and creating career progression plans for team members.
e) Coaching employees to improve operational, analytical, and leadership capabilities.
f) Building a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, customer obsession, and operational excellence.

Process & Operational Excellence

a) The role requires a strong focus on continuously improving AP operations by:
b) Identifying process gaps, inefficiencies, and recurring defects.
c) Performing root-cause analysis and implementing sustainable solutions.
d) Standardizing processes across subsidiaries and geographies.
e) Reducing manual effort through automation and self-service.
f) Improving payment accuracy and timeliness.
g) Driving measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, and customer/vendor experience.
h) Establishing mechanisms to monitor and prevent negative service trends.


Stakeholder Management
a) The candidate will work extensively with Finance, Procurement, Controllership, Internal Audit, Technology, Operations, and external vendors across multiple geographies.
b) The role requires the ability to communicate effectively with senior stakeholders, influence decisions, manage escalations, and drive cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.



A day in the life
What This Role Offers You

You’ll have a front-row seat to Amazon’s financial infrastructure at global scale - leading a team that directly impacts supplier relationships, cash management, and controllership across every marketplace Amazon operates in. This is not a maintain-the-status-quo role: you’ll build new operating models, drive automation, and shape the future of how Amazon pays its partners.


Key Performance Areas

Success in this role will be measured through:

i. Operational Excellence – Accuracy, productivity, quality, and SLA adherence.
ii. Payment Performance – Timely and accurate vendor payments.
iii. People Leadership – Team engagement, performance, retention, and career development.
iv. Process Improvement – Automation, standardization, and measurable efficiency gains.
v. Customer/Vendor Experience – Effective resolution of issues and improvement in service levels.
vi. Controllership & Compliance – Strong internal controls and audit readiness.
vii. Cost Optimization – Productivity improvements and effective resource utilization.
viii. Business Growth & Scalability – Readiness to support new subsidiaries, geographies, volumes, and business requirements.


About the team
About the Team

Accounts Payable Operations supports multiple geographies and marketplaces globally and provides critical financial services across the organization.

The team is responsible for:

1. Manual and automated invoice processing.
2. Invoice ingestion and validation.
3. Resolution of invoice holds and exceptions.
4. Ensuring timely and accurate supplier payments.
5. Vendor account setup and maintenance.
6. Responding to supplier and business partner queries.

title: Community Impact Excellence & Standards (Global Procurement Organization), Global Procurement Community Impact
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon's Global Procurement Sustainability team and build the operating backbone of Community Impact — the strategy, standards, regulations, donations excellence and governance that turn procurement into lives improved impact for communities across 26 countries.

As the owner of Community Impact Excellence & Standards for Global Procurement Organization (GPO) Community Impact (CI), you'll bring strategy, policy, standards, regulatory alignment, compliance, execution excellence, and governance to the full Community Impact program, spanning all five pillars: Supplier for Good, Procurement for Good, Waste to Worth, Space for Good / Donation Hubs, and AI For Good with IDonate. You'll set the standards and standard operating procedures that make impact consistent and compliant everywhere, drive execution to ambitious donation targets (including $10M in procurement donations in 2027), and make Community Impact visible all the way up to senior leadership.

Drive excellence — raise execution quality and consistency of CI programs across 26 countries

Own regulations & compliance — ensure CI activity is compliant, regulation-aligned, and auditable

Lead donations execution — including the Waste to Worth standard operating procedure and the $10M 2027 procurement-donations target

Govern & report — embed CI performance into Monthly Business Review and Quarterly Business Review forums and leadership communications

Set the strategy — shape the multi-year strategy for Community Impact excellence and standards

Key job responsibilities
Strategy — Own and drive the multi-year strategy for Community Impact excellence and standards: define the vision, the roadmap to scale consistency and quality across all five pillars and 26 countries, and the long-term path to a world-class CI operating model.

Standards, Policy & Process — Define and own the GPO CI standards, policy, and process across all five pillars; embed CI requirements into GPO's procurement processes so impact activity is a defined, consistent step across every country rather than ad-hoc and local.

Regulations & Compliance — Own CI regulatory alignment and compliance across all 26 countries; maintain vetting and eligibility standards for NGOs, charities, suppliers, and partners with documented, auditable approval gates so CI activity routes through a compliant, risk-screened pathway.

Execution Excellence (incl. Waste to Worth & Donations) — Ensure quality and consistency of CI program execution across pillars and countries. Within this, lead GPO CI procurement donations (not supplier donations) end-to-end to a $10M 2027 target, and execute the Waste to Worth standard operating procedure (surplus and non-inventory product donations) globally.

Governance & Communication — Own the CI governance cadence: embed CI performance, standards, and compliance into Monthly Business Review and Quarterly Business Review forums, and run the communication plan that keeps Global Procurement Sustainability leadership, GPO leadership, and country stakeholders aligned on CI strategy and targets.

A day in the life
The Community Impact Excellence & Standards role is the owner of excellence, standards, and governance for the full GPO Community Impact (CI) team. Within this remit, the role also leads and owns GPO CI procurement donations end-to-end — not supplier donations — globally across 26 countries, including the Waste to Worth standard operating procedure and its execution, with a target of $10M in donations for 2027. Donations and Waste to Worth are a flagship execution stream inside the broader excellence-and-standards mandate.

title: Software Development Engineer, Promotions Calculations Lifecycle (PCL)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s Worldwide Deals and Promotions organization builds the systems that compute and apply promotional benefits to hundreds of millions of customer orders every day. The Promotions Calculations Lifecycle (PCL) team owns the checkout-time calculation path: deciding which promotions apply to a cart, how benefits combine, and what the customer ultimately pays — correctly, at low latency, and at worldwide scale.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II (SDE II) to own the design, build, and operation of services on this critical path. You will work on high-throughput, low-latency systems where correctness is customer-facing and measured in real money. This is a hands-on engineering role for a builder who enjoys deep technical ownership, solving ambiguous problems with team members, and raising the operational bar for services that must work worldwide on Day 1.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end to end the design, implementation, testing, deployment, and operation of components and services on the promotions calculation path, from design document through post-launch monitoring.
- Design and build scalable, low-latency services and features that compute promotional benefits correctly at checkout for customers worldwide.
- Raise code quality through thorough, timely code reviews, strong testing practices, and secure, maintainable, well-instrumented code.
- Drive operational excellence — participate in on-call, reduce operational load through automation, and constructively identify and fix sources of defects and toil.
- Collaborate across teams with partner engineering teams, product managers, and stakeholders to deliver cross-functional initiatives that span multiple months.
- Work through ambiguity by breaking down loosely defined problems, unblocking yourself and others, and making pragmatic decisions that move the team forward.
- Mentor and uplevel peers and newer engineers through design feedback, pairing, and knowledge sharing.

A day in the life
A typical week combines focused building with the collaboration and operational rigor that keep a Tier-1 service healthy. You might start the day reviewing a design document for a change to how benefits combine at checkout, then pair with a teammate on the Universal Benefit Service (UBS) to reduce calculation latency on a high-traffic path. You will write and review code, add tests and metrics, and ship changes through the team’s continuous deployment pipeline.

You will take part in the on-call rotation for services the team owns, using operational signals to find and remove recurring sources of defects and toil. You will work with partner teams across Worldwide Deals and Promotions, and with product managers, to turn ambiguous requirements into concrete designs. You will also invest in the people around you — giving design feedback, mentoring newer engineers, and sharing what you learn so the whole team levels up.

About the team
The Promotions Calculations Lifecycle (PCL) team sits within Amazon’s Worldwide Deals and Promotions organization. We own the checkout-time path that determines which promotions apply to a customer’s cart, how those benefits combine, and the final price the customer pays. Our services run worldwide and are on the critical ordering path, so correctness, availability, and latency are first-order requirements — the systems we build directly shape both the customer experience and Amazon’s financials.

We are a team of builders who value deep technical ownership, operational excellence, and raising the bar for one another. We invest in mentorship and career growth, work backwards from the customer, and take pride in making complex systems simpler and more reliable over time. You will join a group where your work is highly visible, your decisions matter, and there is ample room to grow as an engineer.

- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience

title: Sr. Associate - Quality Analyst, Global Solutions & Risk Compliance (GSRC)
descriptionHtml:
The Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) organization is a component of Amazon's operations, dedicated to ensuring the compliance of its products and services worldwide. GSRC's core mission is to keep customers, partners, and associates safe while protecting the company from legal and regulatory risks. With a diverse global team spanning across India, China, Poland, Romania, Netherlands, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica, GSRC partners with its stakeholders to classify products and ensure regulatory and legal compliance for product listings. GSRC raises the bar on quality by implementing operational changes matching the everchanging regulatory space. The team designs global, consistent, and scalable solutions and prioritize a blend between technology-driven and human decision-making processes. GSRC believes that innovation thrives on diversity, fostering an inclusive and equitable culture that empowers employees with opportunities for learning and development.

Key job responsibilities
Your job responsibilities as a Sr. Compliance Associate-Quality Analyst may include:
• Performs quality audits on a daily basis using Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and achieves self-utilization, productivity and quality as per defined targets.
• Must be able to comprehend SOPs with minimal support and identify opportunities.
• Identifies anomalies through audits (SOP defects, Process gaps etc.).
• Uses knowledge and identifies defect/s & preliminary root causes, explains the rationale
• Proposes solutions on quality/productivity and work on milestones with managers
• Expertise in research – finding specific information (eg: products, regulations etc) in a timely manner.
• Prepares key insight trends and share reports on regular basis.
• Provide feedbacks to the associates and close loop on audit observations.
• Respond to stakeholders with guidance and flags any updates to Lead/Manager

About the team
Amazon is an E-commerce and Cloud Computing company with headquarters in Seattle, Washington. Since 1995, Amazon has focused on being “the world’s most customer centric company.” Our customers are worldwide, and include not just consumers, but also our sellers and vendors (selling partners). World-class retail brands and individual sellers increase their sales and reach new customers by leveraging the power of the Amazon e-commerce platform. To meet our selling partners’ needs, our smart, diverse, customer-obsessed employees are constantly innovating and building on new ideas.
The Operational Risk Compliance (ORC) organization exists to keep our customers and partners safe, protect associates, and ensure legal and regulatory compliance. We coordinate the aspects of product transactions that are regulated (distribution, shipping, sale, and import/export). Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) is the operational arm of the ORC organization. This involves analyzing product import documentation and flagging hazardous risks. We are also responsible for keeping Amazon customers safe and informed by coordinating actions around worldwide program teams to classify products and ensure Amazon’s product listings follow regulatory and legal compliance guidelines. These actions include removing products from the site and from our warehouses, and contacting customers with pertinent sustainability information. The ORC team partners with GSRC supports regulatory compliance requirements for Amazon’s worldwide programs such as Dangerous Goods, Chemical Safety Compliance, Global Trade Services, Transport Risk Compliance, Sustainability, Extended Producer Responsibility and Food Safety. GSRC has offices across India, China, Poland, Romania, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica and supports compliance related needs for worldwide Amazon marketplaces.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 1+ years of logistics, transportation, supply chain, import/export operations, or data entry/data administration experience
- Knowledge of Excel at a basic level (e.g., UX navigation, math & logical functions, lookup functions, etc.)
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Work 40 hours/week, and overtime as required
- Experience performing accurate data entry and analysis

Preferred qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Bachelor's degree in logistics, transporation, supply chain, or business
- Licensed customs broker
- Experience in international logistics, cross-border transportation and supply chain, or U.S. Customs rules and regulations
- Experience in customs

title: Sr. Associate - Quality Analyst, Global Solutions & Risk Compliance (GSRC)
descriptionHtml:
The Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) organization is a component of Amazon's operations, dedicated to ensuring the compliance of its products and services worldwide. GSRC's core mission is to keep customers, partners, and associates safe while protecting the company from legal and regulatory risks. With a diverse global team spanning across India, China, Poland, Romania, Netherlands, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica, GSRC partners with its stakeholders to classify products and ensure regulatory and legal compliance for product listings. GSRC raises the bar on quality by implementing operational changes matching the everchanging regulatory space. The team designs global, consistent, and scalable solutions and prioritize a blend between technology-driven and human decision-making processes. GSRC believes that innovation thrives on diversity, fostering an inclusive and equitable culture that empowers employees with opportunities for learning and development.

Key job responsibilities
Your job responsibilities as a Sr. Compliance Associate-Quality Analyst may include:
• Performs quality audits on a daily basis using Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and achieves self-utilization, productivity and quality as per defined targets.
• Must be able to comprehend SOPs with minimal support and identify opportunities.
• Identifies anomalies through audits (SOP defects, Process gaps etc.).
• Uses knowledge and identifies defect/s & preliminary root causes, explains the rationale
• Proposes solutions on quality/productivity and work on milestones with managers
• Expertise in research – finding specific information (eg: products, regulations etc) in a timely manner.
• Prepares key insight trends and share reports on regular basis.
• Provide feedbacks to the associates and close loop on audit observations.
• Respond to stakeholders with guidance and flags any updates to Lead/Manager

About the team
Amazon is an E-commerce and Cloud Computing company with headquarters in Seattle, Washington. Since 1995, Amazon has focused on being “the world’s most customer centric company.” Our customers are worldwide, and include not just consumers, but also our sellers and vendors (selling partners). World-class retail brands and individual sellers increase their sales and reach new customers by leveraging the power of the Amazon e-commerce platform. To meet our selling partners’ needs, our smart, diverse, customer-obsessed employees are constantly innovating and building on new ideas.
The Operational Risk Compliance (ORC) organization exists to keep our customers and partners safe, protect associates, and ensure legal and regulatory compliance. We coordinate the aspects of product transactions that are regulated (distribution, shipping, sale, and import/export). Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) is the operational arm of the ORC organization. This involves analyzing product import documentation and flagging hazardous risks. We are also responsible for keeping Amazon customers safe and informed by coordinating actions around worldwide program teams to classify products and ensure Amazon’s product listings follow regulatory and legal compliance guidelines. These actions include removing products from the site and from our warehouses, and contacting customers with pertinent sustainability information. The ORC team partners with GSRC supports regulatory compliance requirements for Amazon’s worldwide programs such as Dangerous Goods, Chemical Safety Compliance, Global Trade Services, Transport Risk Compliance, Sustainability, Extended Producer Responsibility and Food Safety. GSRC has offices across India, China, Poland, Romania, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica and supports compliance related needs for worldwide Amazon marketplaces.
